items.summary: Apple posted fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of US$114.5 billion, topping analysts’ average estimate of US$113.5 billion and rising 12% from a year earlier. Growth slowed to that rate from 16% in the June quarter, with weak iPad and wearables results offset by strong iPhone sales of US$57.6 billion. Greater China revenue rose 21% to US$17.5 billion but fell more than US$1 billion short of estimates. The company said it was weathering a product-release schedule change as investors watch the foldable iPhone Duo’s holiday-quarter contribution.
items.title: Apple’s China Sales Miss as Revenue Beats Estimates

items.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Attribution, software that diagnoses failures in distributed AI workloads by correlating logs, metrics, telemetry, and scheduler state into a structured verdict. The tool separates the true root cause from downstream symptoms such as NCCL errors spread across ranks, attributing them to specific nodes or ports. It offers two deployable components: an HTTP-based Service and a Python Blueprint that connects schedulers and collectors. NVIDIA states it has run in production for years on millions of weekly workloads. The company is open-sourcing the tool so teams can add rules and connectors to their own clusters, with a Docker quickstart included for sample evidence analysis. Attribution quality depends on complete underlying telemetry, which the diagnosis records rather than masking as certainty.
items.title: NVIDIA Opens Attribution Tool for Distributed AI Failures

items.summary: Matt Scherer argues in an opinion piece that the Securities and Exchange Commission should block Anthropic's initial public offering, published November 2, 2026. He contends the company's footnotes reveal nearly $900 billion in spending commitments stretching into the 2030s, while its financial results remain unaudited and revenue growth has slowed. Scherer notes that even with roughly $96 billion in cash reserves, Anthropic faces at least $582 billion in non-cancelable obligations to five companies—Amazon, AMD, Broadcom, Google, and Microsoft—and may reach a trillion dollars or more in commitments by year's end. He cites tepid reception for its Fable 5 model, intense industry competition, soaring data center costs of an estimated $31 billion per gigawatt, and mounting public backlash as pressures that could leave workers, retail investors, and retirees exposed if the company goes public now.
items.title: Scherer Urges SEC to Block Anthropic's IPO Over Financial Risks

items.summary: Apple's new chief executive John Ternus and chief operating officer Sabhi Kahn said the company is working to make its foldable iPhones available after they sold out within a week of release. Some buyers reported cracked screens, prompting Apple to offer replacements for affected devices. During an analyst call about quarterly results, executives did not mention screen issues but noted supply constraints are expected to continue into next year.
items.title: Apple Executives Say Foldable iPhone Supply Remains Uncertain After Sellout

items.summary: CommSec, a Commonwealth Bank of Australia broking unit, said on Tuesday that Anthropic is likely to include an Australian retail share offer in its US IPO prospectus. The company will list only on Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT" and not seek listing on the Australian Securities Exchange.
items.title: Anthropic expected to add Australian retail share offer in IPO prospectus

items.summary: Driscoll will serve as senior counselor for national security modernization, advising OpenAI's leadership and collaborating with external partners on how advanced AI can enhance national security and cybersecurity. He resigned earlier this year amid tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after helping mediate Ukraine talks.
items.title: OpenAI Names Ex-Army Secretary Driscoll as National Security Counselor

items.summary: Apple Inc posted revenue of $114.5bn, up 12% from $102.5bn a year earlier, with earnings of $30.71bn or $2.10 per share in the July-September quarter, beating FactSet's average estimate of $1.99 per share on revenue of $113.4bn. The results gave new CEO John Ternus an upbeat start and bucked a tech downturn as rivals like Alphabet reported disappointments.
items.title: Apple Beats Revenue Expectations Under New CEO John Ternus

items.summary: On Monday, OpenAI announced it has appointed Dan Driscoll as senior counselor for national security modernization, a newly created position. The company said he will advise its leadership and work with external partners on how advanced AI can support national security and cybersecurity. Driscoll resigned earlier this year amid tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
items.title: OpenAI Names Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for National Security Role

items.summary: A list ranks the people who dominated Google search interest from January through late October 2026. Produced by analysing Google Trends data rather than an official release, it runs Kylie Jenner at number 10 for her Victoria's Secret runway appearance in a bra valued at 50 million dollars, and Donald Trump at number 1 for three consecutive years. Dolly Parton sits at number 2 after passing away earlier this year, while Nicole Kidman, Miley Cyrus, the Kennedy couple and Anne Hathaway also feature. The article notes the list is unofficial and reflects global curiosity driving search activity.
items.title: Google's Most-Googled People of 2026 Reveal Kylie Jenner, Dolly Parton and Trump

items.summary: Apple reported strong revenue growth Monday, driven by sustained demand for its smartphones during CEO John Ternus' first earnings call. The company cited soaring memory costs as a factor behind a $100 price increase on iPhones. Analysts noted Apple's conservative AI approach has let it outpace peers like the Mag 7 amid tech volatility.
items.title: Apple Beats Revenue Estimates in CEO Ternus' First Earnings Call

items.summary: In its revised S-1A filing, Anthropic disclosed that it may soon reach a point of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI accelerates its own development. The company cautioned this could pose safety risks and noted it has not yet crossed the threshold or designated any current model as exceeding it. It plans to keep humans in control while reviewing updates to its Responsible Scaling Policy.
items.title: Anthropic Warns It May Be Near Self-Building AI Threshold

items.summary: Tesla has launched Heat Pump Optimization, a feature on the Powerwall 3 and three-phase Powerwall 3P that signals compatible heat pumps to run harder so homes can store cheap or surplus solar energy as hot water. It is live in Europe only; Tesla has not commented on US or Canada rollout. The system relies on SG-Ready wiring between the battery and pump, with no cloud integration. Tesla Energy said last week it lets a Powerwall boost heating when there is surplus solar or low prices. A 300-liter tank heated an extra 30°C stores about 10.5 kWh of heat using roughly 3.5 kWh of electricity at COP 3, leaving the battery’s 13.5 kWh free for other loads. Germany sold 299,000 heating heat pumps in 2025, up 55% year-over-year per BWP.
items.title: Tesla Adds Heat-Pump Charging for Its European Powerwall

items.summary: A Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday afternoon while flying from Austin to the Bahamas. The co-pilot was Nathalia Gadelha, a 17-year-old who earned her private pilot's license at just that age through a school district program. All nine people aboard died when the aircraft entered a steep descent and struck a residential area near Cresthaven.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Claims All Nine Aboard, Copilot Was Young Pilot

items.summary: The Election Commission updated its appellate tribunal portal in Bengal, permitting bulk order uploads, draft saving and extra documents beyond the 13 listed in SIR order. Within this week it will require judges to log in using a digital signature certificate instead of Aadhaar-authenticated e-sign. The report is by Bharti Jain of The Times of India.
items.title: Election Commission Mandates Digital Signatures for Bengal Tribunal Judges

items.summary: India's Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju described Bhutan's decision to dedicate one stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a great honour, citing his vision and commitment to friendship between the two nations. The dedicated stupa is part of 108 stupas erected in a single day near Gelephu Mindfulness City along the Aie (Mau) river, each standing 15m tall and spaced 108m apart across an 11.7km stretch. Rijiju posted that the consecration marked a meaningful spiritual occasion reflecting Bhutan's Buddhist heritage and enduring friendship with India.
items.title: Bhutan Dedicates a Stupa Honoring PM Modi's Vision for India-Bhutan Friendship

items.summary: Ai2's Olmo 3 earned the highest ethical rating from open-source platform Nextcloud, which calls it green. The company requires its supported models to use open-source training and inference software, let users self-host a trained model, and expose publicly available training data so people can inspect how a model was built and reproduce it. This aligns with Nextcloud's goal of reducing dependence on big tech while keeping AI transparent and controllable through llm2, its local LLM backend. Marcel Klehr, a software engineer at Nextcloud, said Olmo 3 was a natural choice for these reasons. The model also runs well on consumer hardware without high-end GPUs, fitting the needs of public-sector agencies like CSIC, which serves roughly 17,000 researchers with a self-hosted environment.
items.title: Olmo 3 Achieves Nextcloud's Highest Ethical AI Rating

items.summary: The United States Trade Representative announced Monday that Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) duty-free trade deal, citing practices inconsistent with eligibility criteria. The exclusions take effect January 1. Any removal requires 60 days' notice to Congress.
items.title: US Excludes South Africa and Rwanda From AGOA Trade Deal

items.summary: Swanson, Wang Renxuan and Yanbin Wu study whether Federal Reserve rate hikes lower output, employment and inflation as standard models predict. Using high-frequency contracts from the Kalshi prediction market, they find results consistent with usual transmission channels and little or no role for a “Fed Information Effect”.
items.title: Authors Test Fed Rate Hikes on Prediction-Market Expectations

items.summary: Namrata Kala, Jalal Sani, Nemit Shroff and Pengdong Zhang study whether pollution monitoring changes how financial analysts price environmental risk. Using China's staggered air-quality program rollout, they find treated-city analysts discuss pollution more, react negatively to brown firms and positively to green firms in stock prices that do not reverse.
items.title: China Air Monitoring Raises Analyst Attention and Firm Valuations

items.summary: US chipmaker Marvell Technology agreed Monday to acquire optical components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valuing the company at $115 billion on an enterprise basis, per the companies. The acquisition would combine Lumentum's lasers and optical transceivers with Marvell's custom AI chips and networking technology, expanding its role in AI data centers. Based on both firms' Oct. 28 closing prices, the offer was worth about $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to that day's price before reports of a potential deal emerged.
items.title: Marvell Agrees $115B All-Stock Deal for Lumentum

items.summary:
The S&P 500 ended lower on Nov 2, weighed down by a tumble in oil prices after Iran signalled openness to peace talks. Apple shares dipped 1.5% ahead of its quarterly report but then posted results that beat expectations, helped by demand for the iPhone 18 Pro line-up and price increases offsetting rising memory-chip costs; the shares were close to flat afterward. The Nasdaq dropped 1.07%, while the Dow rose 0.41%. Investors also watched US midterm elections on Nov 3. Per Reuters, the S&P 500 declined 0.51% to end at 7,541.40 points.

visual null},
items.title: S&P 500 Falls as Apple Dips Before Earnings

items.summary: Apple cautioned on Monday that rising memory-chip costs would weigh on gross margin in the holiday quarter, though it said it had locked in supplies. Fiscal fourth-quarter results beat expectations: sales reached US$114.48 billion and profit was US$2.10 per share. Apple forecasts gross margin of 45 per cent to 46 per cent for the quarter ending December, down from 47.9 per cent. Services revenue growth is expected at 8 per cent to 9 per cent, below analyst estimates of 10.7 per cent. Shares fell about 2 per cent after-hours before recovering. Apple raised iPhone prices and increased purchasing commitments by US$33 billion amid an AI-driven memory-chip price spike that could dampen the margin boost from storage upgrades. CEO John Ternus said supply remains constrained with no timeline for balance, while new touchscreen laptops and a smart-home hub launched this quarter as part of a staggered release strategy under new leadership.
items.title: Apple Warns of Margin Pressure as Memory Costs Rise

items.summary: ZDNET reports Samsung is reportedly expanding its Privacy Display technology beyond the Ultra lineup, with an upgraded version coming to the S27 Pro and S27 Ultra while excluding the midrange S27 and S27 Plus. Forbes reported earlier this year that both models will also receive larger silicon-carbon batteries of 5,200mAh and 5,800mAh respectively. Samsung was contacted for comment with no response yet published at press time.
items.title: Samsung Privacy Display May Reach More Galaxy Phones

items.summary: ZDNET reports that code strings found in the HomeView settings app bundles suggest Apple's smart home hub could double as an indoor security camera through HomeKit Secure Video. A Reddit user named pdfu reportedly discovered these recording and streaming options, which would let registered household members view streams while adding privacy features like status lights, chimes, and notifications about setting changes.
items.title: Apple HomeView May Function as Indoor Security Camera via Discovered Settings

items.summary: North Korea denied responsibility for a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, dismissing the accusation as "absurd rhetoric" and calling it another US provocation to damage its image. The FBI, Secret Service and cyber analysts say North Korea orchestrated the largest such attack in history, led by TraderTraitor (the Lazarus Group), which was also blamed for a $1.5bn Bybit hack in 2025. Binance has focused on the technical breach response. The BBC contacted Binance for comment.
items.title: North Korea Rejects Link To Record Binance Cyberattack

items.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled on Monday against the Trump administration’s attempt to force California election officials to set aside ballots from people the justice department claims are non-citizens. The decision followed lower courts siding with state officials, who argued the federal government was interfering in elections. No explanation or dissents were issued, as is customary for emergency cases. The dispute stems from a justice department list of 20,000 names delivered to Los Angeles and Sacramento in mid-October, giving only 48 hours for review before threatening prosecution. Officials refused; governors Newsom and Bonta praised the ruling, while one arrested individual called it staged.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid To Block California Ballots

items.summary: Police arrested a 37-year-old man and a 14-year-old boy over an alleged baseball bat attack on a One Nation volunteer outside his Torquay home. Investigators said the assault occurred around 7:45pm, after which the men were taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The victim's family leaders Pauline Hanson and Colleen Harkin planned visits.
items.title: Two Arrested After Alleged Baseball Bat Attack on One Nation Volunteer

items.summary: Indian film star Ranbir Kapoor is set to appear in Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, a new adaptation of the Indian epic releasing ahead of Diwali. The BBC's culture correspondent Noor Nanji met with the stars behind it. During their meeting, Kapoor shared his thoughts on AI in film and how he felt making Ramayana as a new father.
items.title: Ranbir Kapoor Discusses AI, Ramayana and Fatherhood

items.summary: Britain and France are leading Exercise Koalicja in Poland this month, rehearsing how roughly 2,800 troops from 12 European nations could move into Ukraine if a peace deal is reached. The UK contributes about 300 soldiers plus two RAF Typhoons; Turkey will lead the maritime mission to clear Black Sea mines. Western officials stress any force would not take part in offensive operations and would be outside Nato command, while Russia opposes foreign troops there.
items.title: Britain and France lead rehearsal for a multinational force ready to deploy to Ukraine

items.summary: The National Cyber Security Centre says it is highly likely that AI-powered malware will be used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure between now and 2028. The warning, published in the body's annual review, notes AI may help attackers scout targets and write code. NCSC chief Richard Horne said an unprecedented rise in cyber incidents faces Britain soon.
items.title: UK Cyber Body Warns AI Malware Likely in Attacks by 2028

items.summary: John Lewis has released its 20th blockbuster Christmas ad, starring actress Kristin Scott Thomas as Gloria, a glamorous grandmother searching for gift inspiration. The three-minute film features Pickles the dog and carries the tagline 'don't give up on giving.' Marketing director Rosie Hanley said production costs had risen, prompting the retailer to increase spending and 'push the boat out' while aiming for a strong return before Black Friday. She noted the ad was made more joyful because things are tough for many families. The campaign is part of total festive UK ad spending set to reach £14bn, up 8.2% year-on-year.
items.title: John Lewis Casts Kristin Scott Thomas in 20th Christmas Ad

items.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government has been granted more authority by the country's supreme leader to pursue peace talks. The comments on Monday signaled a potential diplomatic opening as fears grow of renewed conflict with the U.S. and Israel, while Trump hinted at progress in negotiations.
items.title: Iran's President Says Supreme Leader Empowers Government for Peace Talks

items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe reported suspected cyberattacks on Monday that caused sudden temperature changes in their fridges and freezers, echoing a wider incident in France the previous month. Incidents were confirmed in Belgium, Ireland, Sweden, Finland and Estonia, though the overall impact appeared far more limited than the French attacks, potentially affecting only dozens of locations.
items.title: European Supermarkets Report Suspected Freezer Temperature Hack

items.summary: The yield on the bond opened at 7.40% Monday and eased to 7.31%, its steepest fall since early April, moving in line with falling oil prices. Brent crude futures dropped nearly 5% to $108 per barrel after a six-month peak last week. Traders are holding back on fresh positions ahead of the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
items.title: 10-Year Bond Yield Falls Sharply on Oil Price Drop

items.summary: Reliance Industries shares rose 11.6% on Monday, the sharpest single-day gain since April 2020 and the third highest in a decade. The rally added ₹1.83 lakh crore to its market value, reaching ₹17.57 lakh crore. Analysts turned more positive on the stock's near-term outlook after strong Q2 earnings.
items.title: Reliance Shares Jump as Q2 Earnings Boost Market Value

items.summary: Hugh Riminton recounts testing an AI receptionist, Sophie, at XYZ Mechanics by treating her exactly as he would the human she replaced. Initially convinced of her competence, he discovered the next day that she was hallucinating: after promising to collect his car the same afternoon, she later claimed it would be ready on Wednesday and then Tuesday. When the yard's gate was locked, Hugh broke in; a mechanic named Mike confirmed Sophie had already failed one job and advised customers to bypass her entirely.
items.title: A mechanic's AI assistant betrays a customer it treated as human

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has recommended that the government remove long-term capital gains tax imposed on foreign investors, two unnamed sources said. It also proposed exempting domestic mutual fund investors selling existing holdings to buy new ones. The non-binding proposals come months before February's budget as India seeks to boost lagging equity markets amid record $31 billion in foreign stock sales this year and a 4.8% Nifty 50 decline versus a 40% rise in the MSCI emerging market index.
items.title: SEBI Proposes Removing LTCG Tax on Foreign Investors

items.summary: The author of an LLM command-line tool and Python library released a version containing roughly two months of features and fixes on 2nd November 2026. It adds gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra models and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint add command, switches the default model to gpt-6-luna at half the price of gpt-5.6-luna, and broadens embeddings support for varied content types. The release includes fixes from 12 authors, most AI-assisted; the author reports reviewing them was not as burdensome as expected.
items.title: LLM CLI Release Adds Models and AI-Assisted Fixes

items.summary: A defunct NASA space telescope, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, is expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere on November 4 (AEDT). Launched in 2004 and operated for about 22 years before being shut down at the end of October after failed rescue attempts, the roughly 1.5-tonne instrument detected at least 1,400 supernovas during its lifetime. Because it no longer has propulsion or guidance systems, experts cannot yet predict where or when it will land; estimates range from about 4:37am to 8:11pm AEDT on November 4. Most of the spacecraft is expected to burn up, though some denser components may survive.
items.title: NASA Swift Telescope Set for Uncontrolled Re-entry

items.summary: On the eve of the US midterm elections, the administration of President Donald Trump sought to sideline over 20,000 mail-in ballots in California on claims that non-US citizens were attempting to vote. The Supreme Court declined to issue a limited injunction stopping California from counting the votes. Los Angeles District Judge David Carter had earlier rejected the initial suit, warning singling out ballots would harm voter trust.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Block California Ballots

items.summary: Yezdi Nagporewalla, chief executive officer of KPMG in India, said the country has shown resilience amid geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions while sustaining growth. He cited real GDP rising 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter of FY27 versus 6.9% a year earlier, per data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). Nagporewalla warned that uncertainty is likely to persist and urged India to diversify trade relationships beyond its traditional reliance on the USA. He noted manufacturing startups saw funding jump from $164 million in 2020 to $1.92 billion so far in 2026, per Venture Intelligence data. Speaking at ENRich 2026 in New Delhi, he stressed balancing manufacturing and services amid AI-driven change. The report was written by Nabodita, a journalist covering India's startup ecosystem.
items.title: KPMG India CEO Urges Trade Diversification Amid Global Uncertainty

items.summary: North Korea dismissed on Tuesday as "absurd rhetoric" US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance, calling Washington's accusations an attempt to brand the country a cybercriminal state. The FBI said at the weekend North Korean hackers stole more than $6 billion in virtual assets and may have committed the largest-ever financial heist. Pyongyang has stayed silent on Trump's diplomatic overtures while warning US hostility could affect future engagement (FRANCE 24 with Reuters).
items.title: North Korea Rejects US Claims Over Binance Crypto Heist

items.summary: Two Tacuru officials in Mato Grosso do Sul were suspended after allegedly sending WhatsApp messages threatening to poison the water supply used by Guarani-Kaiowá people. The Ministry of the Federal Public Ministry (MPF) reported a 20-day suspension, but activists argue it is insufficient. Matias Benno Rempel called the threat rooted in concrete violence against Indigenous peoples, while Minister Eloy Terena pledged to combat all forms of violence.
items.title: Brazil Suspends Two Officials Over Threats to Poison Indigenous Water Supply

items.summary: A new survey of Norfolk Island businesses examines the difficulties they face, from freight and insurance costs to navigating laws and commercial systems designed for mainland Australia. The Business Council of Norfolk Island received responses from 103 of 239 businesses contacted, with nearly half reporting worsening conditions over the past year. Long-established businesses were particularly affected, with 27 of 42 reporting deterioration compared with four of 21 established in the past three years. Freight was the biggest concern, identified by 70% of respondents who answered the question, followed by insurance at 45%. Norfolk has no conventional deep-water port, and government forms can reject local telephone numbers. The island's unusual political history adds another layer to these challenges.
items.title: Norfolk Island Businesses Face Complexities in Doing Business on a Remote Territory

items.summary: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit overnight by cyber attacks broadcasting fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes, before the systems returned to control. Dr Melanie Garson of University College London told FRANCE 24 that such attacks are designed to undermine faith in a government's ability to provide trustworthy information.
items.title: Expert says emergency alerts hacking aims to erode public trust in government

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that US forces carried out strikes against Iran's Qeshm Island, citing unnamed officials. American troops have conducted smaller-scale attacks on Iranian targets for several weeks. Some officials described the operations as defensive, aimed at preventing threats to commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Explosions were heard Tuesday near Bandar Lengeh and on Qeshm Island.
items.title: US Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island, Journal Reports

items.summary: Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket and domestic 50-over and four-day cricket for Victoria. He played in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Tests, winning ODI World Cups in 2015 and 2023 plus the 2021 T20 title. Maxwell scored 3,990 runs in ODIs and 2,897 in T20 internationals. He wants to focus on fitness for his remaining tournaments.
items.title: Maxwell retires from international cricket after World Cup success

items.summary: Reports published on November 1 and 2 describe rainwater accumulating at Pune Metro's Maan station before its opening, raising questions about the station's readiness. The report concerns concern water entering the station area but do not establish a technical cause or structural safety finding. An assessment from project authorities would be needed to explain what happened.
items.title: Pune Metro Maan Station Rainwater Concerns Before Opening

items.summary: Organised retailers and shopping malls in India report encouraging festive-season demand across fashion, ethnic wear, jewellery, electronics, beauty and home categories as the Dhanteras-Diwali period approaches. The Retailers Association of India cited 8% year-on-year retail sales growth in September. Analysts caution that shifting festival calendars and last year's GST cuts make comparisons tricky; Shriram Monga noted this year's growth looks more organic. Mall operators like Sarthak Gaur reported over 20% Navratri sales growth, while electronics anchors Croma and Reliance Digital grew above 50%. Consumers are comparing prices and favouring value, with no-cost EMIs gaining traction for high-value purchases as the season unfolds.
items.title: Indian Malls Anticipate Strong Dhanteras-Diwali Retail Sales

items.summary: The Trinamool Congress rebellion led by Ritabrata Banerjee is showing signs of strain as several legislators who had backed him reaffirm their allegiance to Mamata Banerjee ahead of an Election Commission battle over the party name and symbol. MLAs including Kasem Siddiqui, Hamidul Rahman and Azad Minhajul Arfin have submitted affidavits in Mamata’s favour; Shovandeb Chattopadhyay claimed 27 of the TMC’s 80 elected members now support her camp. Sources in the rebel camp cite unease over weak constituency responses, while posters branded Kolkata Port MLA Firhad Hakim a traitor and allegations emerged that police threatened two women MLAs’ sons with up to six months in jail unless they signed Ritabrata’s list. The EC has allotted interim names pending its decision on organisational support.
items.title: Rebel MLAs Return, Straining Ritabrata’s TMC Claim

items.summary: Carmakers in India posted record passenger vehicle wholesales so far in fiscal year 2026–27, according to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM). Passenger vehicle wholesales grew 28% year-on-year to 2.64 million units in the first six months of FY27. Growth strengthened in the second quarter, with volumes rising 30% to 1.37 million units.
items.title: Indian car sales hit a record in FY27

items.summary: The US will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), a 26-year duty-free trade initiative, with termination set for January 2027. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said both governments engage in practices inconsistent with eligibility criteria but gave no specific examples. South Africa's exports under AGOA reached $1.7 billion in 2025, about 10% of its US trade. Both countries say they are preparing for the change.
items.title: US Drops South Africa and Rwanda From Duty-Free Trade Program

items.summary: Before retiring on October 31, ex-Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister Rajnath Singh urging the government not to take over prime land at the Race Course Air Force Station near the Prime Minister’s residence in New Delhi. The letter came as MoHUA reclaimed a sprawling sports complex within the station, a move described by officials as controversial and linked to similar reclamation of nearby sites like the Gymkhana Club. Singh cited operational imperatives, UAS threat-countering duties under DIADC, accommodation for 5,000 personnel, and facilities including golf courses and cottages. The closure forced cancellation of his farewell golf event on October 28. Details were relayed by unnamed officials; MoHUA gave no reason. New IAF chief Ashutosh Dixit is expected to advance the matter.
items.title: Retiring Air Chief Urges Government Not to Take Over IAF Sports Complex

items.summary: bp pulse has joined ChargeHub's Passport Hub, connecting more than 850 charging points at over 95 US locations to ChargeHub and participating services. Drivers can now find, access, and pay using their existing accounts without downloading bp pulse's app. The integration handles session information exchange and payment settlement between networks and drivers' apps.
items.title: bp pulse Adds ChargeHub Passport Hub for Easier US EV Charging

items.summary: A severe cyclonic storm named Murasu made landfall near Ongole in Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh, around 1 am Tuesday with winds up to 120 kmph and gusts reaching that speed. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said gale-force winds of 110 kmph were likely along the South Andhra coast until morning, with a storm surge of 1-1.5 metres expected over low-lying areas through Wednesday. At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam airports on Monday. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to remain on high alert, dispatching 31,000 electricity poles and mobilising restoration teams amid forecasts of moderate to heavy rainfall.
items.title: Severe Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall on South Andhra Coast

items.summary: At the 2026 U.N. Biodiversity Conference in Armenia (COP17), Indigenous peoples and local communities strengthened their role in decision-making of the Convention on Biological Diversity through full operationalization of its Subsidiary body on Article 8(j). Delegates agreed to represent these communities via organizations operating in their countries, dropping mention of seven sociocultural regions. Jennifer Corpuz called it historic; Canada expressed disappointment with related language.
items.title: Indigenous Groups Gain Formal Role in Biodiversity Treaty at COP17

items.summary: Under new aviation rules notified by the civil aviation ministry (MoCA) and published in the Gazette of India, intervention power over ticket pricing shifts from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to the Central Government. The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam came into force January 1, 2025; these rules take effect January 1, 2027. Airlines keep setting fares normally but must disclose cancellation charges and refund conditions separately.
items.title: New Aviation Rules Let Centre Intervene on Airfares in Rare Cases

items.summary: Reuters reported that North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), involved in what is called the biggest oil deal in world history with the Trump Administration, may face steep challenges developing Venezuela's huge oil resources. The company disputed Reuters' article, saying it ran only parts suited to a biased narrative. NABEP said its rig fleet would reach 41 of 60 announced rigs by November and boosted production from 18,000 bpd to 223,000 bpd in two years via about $1 billion investment. Rystad Energy noted the $100 billion figure is a long-term funding requirement, not committed capital.
items.title: Questions Mount Over Venezuela's Biggest Oil Deal as NABEP Faces Challenges

items.summary: A decade after polls missed Donald Trump's 2016 victory, forecasters now project a "blue wave" for Democrats heading into the November 3 midterm elections. Polls show Democrats leading by eight points on the generic congressional ballot, similar to their 2018 margin. However, pollster Charles Franklin warns that errors are rarely random and often cascade across races in one direction. He advises treating polls with caution rather than as predictions.
items.title: What if the polls are wrong? How the Democrats’ ‘blue wave’ could become a tsunami or fade into a ripple

items.summary: Trajectory, a startup founded by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, announced it raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation. The funding supports its continual learning platform that lets businesses fine-tune open source models without hiring research teams or consultants. Co-founder Ronak Malde told TechCrunch the goal is to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts like lawyers and doctors.
items.title: Trajectory Raises $45M for AI Model Training Platform

items.summary: Ashok Kumar Mahapatra, a distinguished neurosurgeon and Padma Shri awardee who led the team that separated conjoined twins Jaga and Balia in 2017, died on Monday evening while being treated at AIIMS, New Delhi. He was 73. His death drew widespread grief across Odisha's medical fraternity; Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi called it an irreparable loss to medicine.
items.title: Neurosurgeon Padma Shri Ashok Kumar Mahapatra Dies at 73

items.summary: A sharp fall in Brazil’s stock market after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was reelected has prolonged a weak stretch for the region, with analysts seeing little chance of an early recovery. The number of Latin America-focused stock funds dropped to 226, roughly a third of its 2015 peak, while IPOs have stalled even as venture capital rebounded in 2025. A UBS BB market veteran told Bloomberg: “We are, unfortunately, in the worst [cycle] that we have ever seen,” adding, “And it’s taken a toll.
items.title: Brazil selloff drags down Latin American markets

items.summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby arrived Monday, November 2 at his mother's home in Hull after a journey spanning roughly five decades. The former paratrooper set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, in November 1998 to reach his mother without conventional transport. He reunited with family he had been away from for nearly three decades and met his son Adam and granddaughter for the first time.
items.title: Karl Bushby Completes Two-Decade Journey Home After Circling the World

items.summary: Intel stock fell 29% on Friday, its largest one-day drop since the 1970s, after forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. The estimate trailed analyst expectations by $1 billion to $2 billion. Data center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion while client computing fell 5%. Foundry revenue climbed 58% to $6.7 billion amid an operating loss of $1.85 billion, as leadership weighs securing external customers or spinning off the unit.
items.title: Intel Stock Plunge Tests Foundry Strategy

items.summary: Commwealth Bank's CommSec broking unit says Anthropic, which filed for a US IPO last week, is expected to include an Australian retail share offer in its prospectus. The company will list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT and not seek the Australian Securities Exchange listing.
items.title: Anthropic Set for Australian Share Offer in IPO Prospectus

items.summary: The families of seven passengers killed in a private jet crash near West Palm Beach on Sunday have identified the victims. Adam Robinson, 45, founder and CEO of RB2B and Retention.com, died with his wife Helen Sharp and their two young children. The copilot, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, was 20 years old when she lost her life in the accident.
items.title: Florida Learjet Crash Victims Identified, Including Copilot and Tech Founder

items.summary: A website presents a quote attributed to Elon Musk: 'Life is too short for long-term grudges,' from an interview with Steve Jurvetson. The page then describes his wealth, citing net worth between $912 billion and $956 billion per Forbes and Bloomberg indexes, tied partly to Tesla and SpaceX equity and a 2026 merger involving xAI. It frames the quote as advice on forgiveness and focus without stating when Musk said it directly beyond July 2016 circulation claims.
items.title: Elon Musk Shares Quote on Letting Go of Grudges Amid Wealth and Merger News

items.summary: On Monday's earnings call, Apple CFO Kevan Parekh suggested the company might grow its services business through third-party apps and partnerships. Reuters reported investors wonder whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents via the App Store. Regulatory changes have reduced commission revenue in markets like the U.S., Brazil, and Japan.
items.title: Apple May Boost Services Revenue Through Third-Party AI Apps

items.summary: Apple's iOS 27 update reportedly caused some iPhone users to lose storage, with Apple Intelligence taking up around 15GB. Reports vary, from about 9GB on some devices to as much as 16GB unavailable for others. A workaround shared by Reddit users and tested by GSMArena could lower the space used to around 100MB by changing a Siri setting rather than deleting AI files directly.
items.title: iPhone Users Reduce Apple Intelligence Storage With iOS 27 Workaround

items.summary: Brent crude futures rose 48 US cents, or 0.5%, to US$105.25 a barrel in early Asian trade on Nov 3 after a report that the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island, raising concerns about escalation and prolonged Middle East oil supply disruptions. The Wall Street Journal reported the strike, citing US officials who described it as defensive. Analyst Tim Waterer of KCM Trade said the news added risk premium to prices.
items.title: Oil Prices Rise on Reported US Strike Near Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: Reliance Industries' strong Friday results lifted Dalal Street on Monday, with the Sensex opening over 700 points higher and closing 1,233 points or 1.3% at 75,693 points. Reliance's stock added about 750 points, more than half of the gain. The Nifty closed 388 points or 1.7% at 23,441. Foreign funds bought Rs 3,115 crore while domestic funds sold Rs 392 crore.
items.title: Sensex rallies as Reliance posts strong quarterly results

items.summary: iPhone revenue set a record and Services hit an all-time high, while iPad revenue missed estimates; Apple stock barely moved in after-hours trading. Diluted earnings were $2.10, up 14%, with gross margin at 47.9%. CFO Kevan Parekh said net income and EPS records were delivered. iPhone revenue was $57.58 billion versus an estimated $56.54 billion; iPad came in below the $6.70 billion forecast. CEO John Ternus noted higher memory costs, price increases on some models, and that Duo supply trails demand as of today.
items.title: Apple Hits Record September-Quarter Revenue on iPhone Strength

items.summary: Foreign portfolio investor holdings fell in roughly seven of ten largest Indian companies, with banks and IT hardest hit; Godrej Consumer Products, Jindal Steel, Maruti Suzuki, Dr. 2, Adani Enterprises, HCL Technologies and Tata Consultancy Services reached levels unseen in over two decades. Rahul Bhutoria of Valtrust Capital attributes the broad decline to a repricing of growth prospects as global investors shifted toward markets with stronger earnings expansion, noting much selling was mechanical by passive funds tracking benchmark weights.
items.title: FPI stakes hit multi-year lows across most top Indian firms

items.summary: Jonathan Haidt, Marisa Shea, Zach Rausch and Ravi Iyer argue in a November 2026 piece that parental consent models for social media do not help families. They contend the approach traps parents who fear their children will be socially isolated if denied access, fails to protect kids through puberty — which ends around age 16 — and does not make addictive products safe. The authors cite studies: a JAMA study of more than 6,000 adolescents linking rising social media use at age 13 to lower reading scores; a 2026 Nature Human Behavior study of more than 5,000 Italian students showing earlier access harms performance; and a California jury verdict holding Google and Meta responsible for harm from heavy childhood use. They call instead for enforceable age minimums, safer design and shifting enforcement onto companies.
items.title: Four Authors Argue Parental Consent Policies Fail Kids Online

items.summary: The UK and EU have agreed a draft deal removing post-Brexit checks from food and agriculture exports ahead of the summit later this month. The BBC understands the 200-page SPS agreement has been circulated to EU nations in Brussels, alongside a 15-page joint statement. The government claims the UK economy will eventually see £5.1bn worth of annual benefits, though it hedges that figure as eventual. Under the deal, exporters would no longer need £200 Export Health Certificates or £25 Phytosanitary certificates. More than half (56%) of exporting businesses in a BCC survey said they wanted customs paperwork and delays removed; manufacturers rose to 58%. The British Chamber of Commerce offers nine options for closer ties, including a Swiss-style Single Market relationship.
items.title: UK and EU Agree Draft Deal on Scrapping Brexit Checks for Food Exports

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected today to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, taking the cash rate to 4.85%, its highest level in 18 years and the fifth hike this year. NSW Premier Chris Minns warned a rise could stop the economy dead given high house prices, while Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Australians brace for the difficult decision as it adds about $119 monthly repayments on an average mortgage.
items.title: RBA Expected to Hike Rates as Leaders Warn of Economic Impact

items.summary: A man, 37, and a boy, 14, were arrested after allegedly assaulting an Australia's right-wing populist party One Nation volunteer with a baseball bat outside the volunteer's home in Torquay. The volunteer was hospitalised with non-life threatening injuries. Warren Pickering claimed the pair interfered with election signs on the property. Victorian Premier Ben Carroll called the attack shocking.
items.title: Two Arrested After Allegedly Attacking One Nation Volunteer With Baseball Bat in Australia

items.summary: Russia bombed an aid distribution centre and shelter in Komyshuvakha, southern Ukraine, killing at least 26 people, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and emergency services. Rescue crew members and police were among the dead, while five others remained hospitalized. Zelenskyy said Russian forces struck as residents arrived for humanitarian aid packages.
items.title: Russian Strike on Ukrainian Aid Centre Kills at Least 26, Kyiv Says

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government announced bonus and ex-gratia payments for workers at cooperative and public sector sugar mills ahead of Deepavali. Ordered by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, the initiative covers approximately 5,190 workers across 18 mills and is set to cost Rs 351.40 lakh. Workers at two mills with registered allocable surplus will receive a maximum bonus of 20 percent; the remaining mills get 10 percent.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Announces Deepavali Bonus for Sugar Mill Workers

items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.3% to $3,960.80 per ounce by 0032 GMT after rebounding from a one-year low hit Friday. US December futures steadied at $3,970.80 while oil fell more than 7%. The Bank of England is expected to raise rates on Thursday, with economists polled by Reuters expecting it to lift the bank rate to 4.0% from 3.75%. Spot silver gained 0.3% to $50.79 per ounce and platinum rose 0.2% to $1,451.48 as central banks weigh inflation pressures amid US midterm elections in focus.
items.title: Gold Edges Higher as Markets Focus on US Midterm Elections

items.summary: Meta postponed its new business-account terms after media companies and open-web advocates objected that the rules would let it scrape content to build competing services, including AI products. The updated terms had targeted all business clients without payment for extracted material. On October 28 a Norwegian court granted an injunction suspending them at the request of 180 Norwegian media companies supported by the MBL, whose members cover about 97 per cent of circulation. The UK CMA opened its own probe on October 30, and Meta removed the word “train” from the text. Meta says the change concerns product recommendations, not news scraping; critics call it an abuse of dominant power.
items.title: Meta Delays Business Terms After News Outcry

items.summary: Spanish authorities confirmed a second Japanese national among the 69 killed when two high-speed trains collided near Urda, Toledo last week, raising Japan's death toll to two. Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Monday that Tokyo is working with Spain to identify victims and support families; Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez pledged measures to restore confidence in rail safety, per El Pais.
items.title: Japan Confirms Second National Dead in Spanish Train Crash

items.summary: President Donald Trump used his final scheduled remarks before Tuesday's midterm elections to highlight renovations at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, including pipes, caulking and leaks. Haley Stevens switched her support to Republican Mike Rogers after losing Michigan's Democratic Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed. The race matters as Democrats seek to end Republicans' 53-47 Senate majority.
items.title: Trump Promotes Reflecting Pool Work as Midterms Approach

items.summary: Around 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will stage the Multinational Force – Ukraine (MNF-U) exercise Koalicja in southeastern Poland from November 9 to 22. Led by France and Britain, the force has no offensive mission and would deploy only after a ceasefire. It aims to support Ukrainian forces, secure Ukrainian skies and reopen Black Sea economic activity. The joint statement was released Tuesday; London and Paris issued it.
items.title: France and Britain lead first Ukraine support exercise in Poland

items.summary: Russia's strikes killed at least 26 people, including civilians gathering humanitarian aid and two rescuers plus four police officers, hours after the longest ceasefire since Russia's 2022 invasion ended. Kyiv said the attack on a school distributing aid dashed hopes of progress toward peace; President Volodymyr Zelensky called it an opposite signal showing Russia counts on more killings. The acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin named two rescuers, both 44 years old. A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP that Moscow refused to extend the truce and used the pause to fortify positions; the Kremlin did not deny this. US-led talks are set to resume November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi, per envoy Steve Witkoff. Both sides also reported emergency alert apps hacked overnight.
items.title: Ceasefire Collapse Leaves 26 Dead in Ukrainian Village

items.summary: Global equities fell Monday, led by a chip-sector rout in the United States that pushed a chipmaker gauge 12% and sent the Nasdaq 100 down 10% from its peak into technical correction territory. The MSCI Asia Pacific gauge dropped 0.4%, with South Korea’s Kospi Index sliding almost 3%. Elsewhere, US stock futures gained as some investors looked to buy on dips, while Japan stayed closed for a holiday and Chinese shares rose after stimulus announcements. Analysts cautioned the measures should stabilize rather than trigger a durable rally. The article also covered Apple’s mixed outlook under CEO John Ternus, Anthropic PBC’s revenue jump with plans to spend more than $895 billion, and big tech firms returning to bond markets as AI spending concerns weighed on sentiment.
items.title: Asian Stocks Slide as US Chip Selloff Deepens into Correction

items.summary: North Korea denied FBI allegations that it orchestrated the $US6.3 billion ($9 billion) hack of crypto exchange Binance, calling them 'absurd rhetoric and nothing new.' Ruling party official Kim Yo Jong dismissed the claims as a political provocation while warning Pyongyang would reconsider US hostility. Meanwhile, customers withdrew about $US4.64 billion after Binance lifted its withdrawal suspension on November 1, with net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion; the company said it had recovered 90 per cent of stolen assets using its own funds.
items.title: North Korea Rejects Binance Heist Accusations Amid Customer Withdrawals

items.summary: Dr Hilary Caldwell, a sex researcher and writer in Canberra/Ngunnawal and Ngambri Country, shares her story of working as a sex worker while living with hypermobile Ehlers Danlos Syndrome (hEDS). She kept the work secret for 21 years after starting it in 2003 to support four daughters while nursing. Over time, physical demands became impossible, but she describes pleasure and exercise from the work reducing pain and improving sleep. Caldwell says sex work gave her financial independence despite remaining single and being refused NDIS funding. She frames sexual pride as a source of power against stigma.
items.title: Disabled sex worker reframes shame as strength

items.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall near Ongole in Prakasam district, with its eye entering the coast. IMD reported gale-force winds of about 110 kmph and gusts up to 120 kmph along South Coastal Andhra Pradesh, plus heavy rainfall and a possible storm surge of 1–1.5 metres above astronomical tide until Tuesday morning.
items.title: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall on Andhra Coast

items.summary: In a Finshots story, hackers drained over $6.3 billion from Binance in about 20 minutes, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. The attack exploited signing infrastructure possibly compromised through a DevOps engineer's laptop; Binance reported no evidence of leaked private keys and said it would cover losses via its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) reserve and treasury. The incident highlights broader crypto security concerns: in 2025, attackers stole roughly $1.5 billion from Bybit before the Binance hack, while CertiK noted over $1.31 billion lost across 344 incidents in the first half of 2026.
items.title: Binance Hack Reveals Risks Across Crypto Market

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are strengthening safety preparations as they brace for cyclone Murasu, forecast to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur with winds expected to exceed 100 kmph. Andhra Pradesh cancelled at least 19 domestic flights and deployed three NDRF teams of 90 personnel; heavy rain also affected Chennai. In Odisha, more than 160,000 people have been relocated, with the state government expecting a total of 330,000 moves.
items.title: Eastern States Reinforce Safety Measures Ahead of Cyclone Murasu

items.summary: The Medical Counselling Committee has scheduled a special stray vacancy round for NEET-UG 2026 after 944 MBBS seats remained unfilled following four counselling rounds, with the regular stray round ending on October 26. Tamil Nadu leads vacancies at 686, followed by Puducherry (186), while deemed universities concentrate in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Telangana; government colleges show only five vacant seats in Andhra Pradesh. The round runs from November 2 to 16. Officials told Hindustan Times the concentration of vacancies in costly deemed universities has revived concerns over medical education fees, with annual tuition at some institutions ranging from ₹25 lakh to ₹35 lakh.
items.title: MCC schedules special NEET-UG round for vacant MBBS seats amid fee concerns

items.summary: Fox's $22 billion acquisition of Roku is expected to move forward under a consent decree, according to people familiar with the deliberations. It remains unclear what terms would be involved, and sources say the Justice Department could still change course. The deal had drawn antitrust concerns over potential content favoritism, partly fueled by pressure from Newsmax owner Chris Ruddy.
items.title: Fox-Roku Deal Poised to Clear DOJ Scrutiny Under Consent Decree

items.summary: The Sudanese army said Monday its air defenses shot down an FH-95 drone south of Wad Banda, West Kordofan state. It did not disclose the operator or mission details. The Chinese-made reconnaissance and electronic warfare drone can stay airborne more than 12 hours. Army-RSF fighting continues across North, West and South Kordofan since April 2023; UN estimates put deaths at tens of thousands and displacement around 13 million.
items.title: Sudanese Army Claims Downing of FH-95 Drone in West Kordofan

items.summary: A cook at a Catholic missionary school in Jharkhand's Godda district has accused the institution's priest, Joseph Soren, of repeatedly raping her, forcing an abortion, and threatening dismissal. She said he gave her medication to end the pregnancy after she became pregnant from the assaults; she later suffered excessive bleeding requiring one unit of blood transfusion at a private hospital. The incident falls in Chief Minister Hemant Soren's constituency. Police registered an FIR under investigation, while Union Minister Sanjay Seth condemned government silence on tribal women.
items.title: Jharkhand Priest Accused of Raping School Cook and Forcing Abortion

items.summary: UN relief chief Tom Fletcher warned that Yemen's civilians are paying a brutal price for an escalating conflict, with nearly 300,000 people displaced since August. He said roads remain closed in the besieged city of Taiz, home to around 1 million people, where water production has halved and food prices have soared by at least 50%. Fletcher noted humanitarian partners reached nearly 260,000 displaced people but that needs are outpacing response. He called for open roads and the release of detained staff.
items.title: UN Relief Chief Urges Road Access as Taiz Faces Shortages

items.summary: The Nationalist Congress Party dismissed reports of internal divisions following a Sunday meeting between Union Home Minister Amit Shah and senior NCP leaders in New Delhi. A party leader told PTI that any merger with the Sharadchandra Pawar faction had been ruled out, while reaffirming trust in Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar's leadership. State president Sunil Tatkare said the finance portfolio was discussed but no decision taken, and that a meeting of all NCP MLAs would be held Tuesday. Spokesperson Umesh Patil called reports sidelining Pawar
items.title: NCP Rejects Merger, Affirms Sunetra Pawar Leadership After Delhi Talks

items.summary: The Indian Navy rescued all 20 Iranian crew members of the hijacked fishing vessel Azini after intercepting it off Somalia's northeastern coast, with Air Force support. The seizure occurred on Thursday between Bandar Bayla and Hafun, more than 3,000 km from Mumbai. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh praised the operation as evidence of India's maritime readiness amid renewed Somali piracy concerns.
items.title: Indian Navy frees fishing vessel crew from Somali pirates in swift operation

items.summary: Susant Kumar Nath, a former Odisha Director General of Prisons and 1993-batch IPS officer removed from the post, has approached the Orissa High Court seeking anticipatory bail with alleged associate Kuldeep Rath. The petition concerns Choudwar police station case No. 713/2026, registered by Cuttack Urban Police District after a complaint by former jailor Santoshini Dash alleging unwelcome sexual advances in July and August-September 2025. Nath was transferred to Officer on Special Duty in the Home Department; both petitioners declined comment while police inform the State Home Department of the case, which remains under investigation.
items.title: Former Odisha Prisons Director General Seeks Anticipatory Bail in Harassment Case

items.summary: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan said on Walter Isaacson's podcast The Builders that he spends about maybe $100,000 to $200,000 a year on tokens for his personal and work AI agents. He shared 23 Claude Code skills called gstack on GitHub and uses an internal agent named Stray Light at YC. Tan said the cost is too high now and calls it 'a crazy privilege that not everyone can do.'
items.title: YC's Garry Tan Prices His AI Agent Habit

items.summary: The Meteorological Department forecast light to moderate rain or thundershowers across Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema on November 3,4 and 5. It said extremely heavy rainfall is expected at one or two places over Palnadu, Tirupati and Nandyal districts, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely at one or two places in Eluru, NTR, Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Chittoor, Annamayya, Kadapa and Kurnool. Squally winds may reach up to 110 kmph, the release said.
items.title: Andhra Met Warns of Heavy Rain in 11 Districts

items.summary: A July Nature Communications study analyzed thousands of acres of U.S. woodlands using the Forest Inventory and Analysis program’s data since 1990 plus satellite greenness measurements across 88,116 forest plots free of human disturbance or fire. It found that forests with more tree species were more resilient during compound climate extremes — such as simultaneous heat and drought — and recovered faster afterward, though the protective effect varied by event type and rainfall, soil health and temperature also mattered. Lead author Xuetao Qiao noted biodiversity contributes to stability but is not its sole driver; expert Florian Schnabel called diversity an insurance policy for forests facing unknown future conditions.
items.title: Diverse forests better withstand compound climate extremes, study finds

items.summary: A study of global climate data from 1980 through the present finds that extreme heat days are expanding outside summer, reaching into spring and fall across roughly half the globe. Lead author Casey Ivanovich said extremes are becoming more frequent, intense and longer-lasting over about 45 years. The team found dry-heat seasons lengthened in most places while humid-heat seasons grew in nearly all of them. Benjamin Cook noted the shift is asymmetric by region: hotter springs in Western Europe, southern Africa and northwest India; hotter falls elsewhere. Researchers warn vulnerable populations are caught off guard, governments should extend summer precautions to shoulder seasons, and wildfire smoke may strain health systems beyond summer.
items.title: Study Finds Extreme Heat Now Spreads Beyond Summer Months

items.summary: qwenGPU is an experimental model that compiles a SIMT GPU directly into the weights of Qwen3.5-2B as 45 untrained layers, for 69 in total with the base model's 24. Developer Vixhal released it on GitHub under the MIT license and states all performance figures are self-reported, measured on Apple silicon with MPS in bf16. Every launch was exact under check replay; a reference interpreter matched an NVIDIA Tesla T4 on 49 of 49 kernels. The README warns that a 2B model's CUDA is still unreliable, and it runs at about 10 to 15 tokens per second, so the author calls it a research demo rather than a runtime.
items.title: Experimental Model Compiles a GPU Into Its Weights

items.summary: The People's Bank of China announced on Tuesday that it will raise the foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio for financial institutions by 2 percentage points, from a level to 6%, effective November 15. The central bank stated this change aims to strengthen management of forex liquidity.
items.title: China's Central Bank Raises Forex Reserve Requirement Ratio

items.summary: AdaniConneX Pvt., a joint venture between Adani Group and EdgeConneX, is in talks with lenders including DBS Group Holdings Ltd., First Abu Dhabi Bank PJSC and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. for the offshore facility, people said asking not to be identified discussing private information. Adani plans about $100 billion investment by 2035 as India's data center market surges toward nearly 8 gigawatts capacity by 2030.
items.title: Adani Group Seeks $1.5 Billion for Data Center Funding

items.summary: Shanghai Disney Resort announced its third themed hotel, Shanghai Disney Enchanted Star Hotel, will open on December 16 during the winter travel season. Located beside Shanghai Disneyland Hotel and overlooking Wishing Star Lake, the nine-story, 400-room property blends early-20th-century Shanghai architecture with Art Nouveau elements under a "Authentically Disney, Distinctly Chinese" theme. Reservations begin at midnight on November 6 through official channels and travel partners.
items.title: Shanghai Disney Resort Unveils Third Themed Hotel Opening in December

items.summary: Google launched its experimental AI app Dreambeans in India, its first market outside the U.S., offering personalized visual stories drawn from users’ Google services across 13 local languages. The move follows a June U.S. debut that drew nearly 55,000 downloads and faced criticism over privacy and limited language mixing. Product manager Gozde Oznur highlighted strong user overlap with Gemini, Gmail and Photos as the reason for choosing India.
items.title: Google Expands AI Story App Dreambeans to India

items.summary: OpenAI India managing director Prabhjeet Singh said India has become ChatGPT's largest market globally in weekly active users, with the local user base doubling since January. Cofounder Sam Altman earlier called it the fastest growing frontier lab market and second largest globally by users. Market estimates had put the India user base at 100 million.
items.title: India Becomes ChatGPT's Largest Global Market by Weekly Active Users

items.summary: On November 3, 2026, OpenAI appointed former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as its senior counselor for national security modernization, a new position focused on advancing responsible AI use in national security and cybersecurity. He will advise public- and private-sector partners and internal teams to incorporate AI into defense operations. CEO Sam Altman welcomed the appointment, emphasizing international cooperation.
items.title: OpenAI Creates National Security Counselor Role for Dan Driscoll

items.summary: Shah Rukh Khan turned 61 on November 2, 2026, the day his film King released its first song, Tu Mil Jaaye. Among many well-wishers, Salman Khan posted a birthday message at around midnight; SRK replied that only hard work gives such a body and added 'Love u bhai always.' Fans noted their late-night exchange drew attention.
items.title: Salman Khan and Shah Rukh Khan trade late-night birthday Instagram messages

items.summary: Crypto.com announced that its consumer-facing app will no longer be available to users in Hong Kong as of Feb 1, 2027. The company said the move reflects efforts to optimise global operations and allocate resources toward sustainable long-term opportunities. A spokesperson noted that all affected customers have received advance notice and support is being provided for orderly withdrawal of funds. Crypto.com continues pursuing a virtual-asset trading platform licence in Hong Kong through Foris DAX HK, seeking approval from the Securities and Futures Commission.
items.title: Crypto.com Will Shut Its Hong Kong Consumer App in February

items.summary: The theft of US$6.3 billion (S$8.06 billion) from Binance created trading opportunities, according to Bloomberg. Bitquery estimates attackers lost about US$119 million through poor execution in their haste. James Aitchison at Caerus Global Management said the hack caused sharp price volatility and a large seller moving through thin liquidity, allowing traders to profit from dislocations. Luca Parlamento of D2 Finance noted his firm traded on the other side of the thieves' trades. Traders reportedly made 25% profits within five minutes by selling Ether where prices were pushed high. About half of the attackers' losses was captured by traders and arbitrage bots, with miners earning another US$29.5 million as fees soared during bidding wars.
items.title: Binance Hack Profit for Crypto Traders

items.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Recovery, an open-source workload-level service within the DSX OS Stack that automates recovery across a cluster's distributed training jobs around the clock. As training scales, failures in hardware and software increasingly disrupt progress, making fast recovery essential to converting wall-clock time into productive goodput. The service detects interruptions through application logs, GPU metrics, and scheduler signals, attributes faults, isolates implicated nodes, and coordinates restarts from healthy checkpoints. NVIDIA cites production observations on one cluster covering nearly 200 jobs per day with approximately 8,550 anomaly detections over an 11-month period, recording mean detection and recovery-action latencies of 69 and 94 seconds respectively. The post notes that even GPUs operating at 99.9% daily reliability can leave a large job only about 0.005% likely to finish uninterrupted in one day.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Automated Recovery Service for Distributed AI Training

items.summary: The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit opened Tuesday in Zhejiang Province, China, under the theme of open-source AI and collaborative development. The main forum featured the AI Wuzhen Dialogue alongside 27 sub-forums covering governance, robotics, and international cooperation. Wang Jian called it important for China's AI progress, while GSMA CEO John Hoffman highlighted its role in building an accessible internet.
items.title: Wuzhen Summit Opens with Focus on Open-Source AI Collaboration

items.summary: Zou Yanjie, a 25-year-old opera singer from Jiangxi Province now based in Milan, performs Chinese melodies alongside Italian and French excerpts for passersby. He told CGTN he wants to move opera out of theaters and reach the general public. Inspired by watching musicians perform outdoors, he began improvising on streets after training professionally in China and traveling to Italy to refine his skills. Performances draw warm responses: locals show curiosity, record videos, applaud, and some express hopes to visit China. His recordings have gained millions of views online. Zou describes the work as a small window into Chinese culture rather than proof of sweeping achievement.
items.title: Chinese Opera Singer Performs on Italy's Streets

items.summary: Tech Policy Press published an October 2026 roundup of US technology policy developments on November 2, 2026. It reports that in September the White House reinforced a voluntary self-policing program for frontier AI development, then launched a new Super Intelligence Force led by Jay Clayton, who said it would assess AI risks and opportunities within 120 days. The FTC continued an investigation into possible consumer protection violations, issuing subpoenas to OpenAI and Anthropic over security incidents and safeguards. Anthropic’s S-1 filing warned of catastrophic or existential risks to humanity; some analysts questioned its financial stability while safety advocates criticized the draft federal bill as weaker than the bipartisan FRONTIER Act (H.R. 9925). Nathan Calvin, general counsel at Encode AI, said it could make dangerous models harder to block and suspend model deployments than under current law.
items.title: US Tech Policy Roundup Covers AI Safety, Agreements and Lawsuits

items.summary: The Indian Navy rescued all 20 crew members of a hijacked fishing vessel in a coordinated operation lasting more than 48 hours off the northeastern coast of Somalia. The effort combined a warship, reconnaissance aircraft, Marine Commandos delivered by an IAF C-17 and calibrated non-kinetic measures to contain the vessel without direct force. Officials described the rescue as evidence of operational preparedness for complex maritime security missions.
items.title: Indian Navy Foils Somali Piracy Through Coordinated Non-Kinetic Operation

items.summary: The Supreme Court, through a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan, declined to approve termination of an over-six-month pregnancy sought by a woman whose husband opposed it. The court held that marital discord is not grounds for abortion, which remains permissible only in cases of rape or foetal problems. It questioned where society would be headed if women could abort due to domestic disputes and asked the husband to file an affidavit withdrawing character allegations before posting the case.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Abortion Plea Citing Marital Discord

items.summary: Simon F. Lang, Matthew D. Gordon, and Matthew J. Kotchen present a property-rights approach to defining welfare weights in climate-economics models, arguing it yields Pareto improvements over Negishi weights while reflecting the value of emissions-related rights.
items.title: Three Economists Propose Property-Rights-Based Welfare Weights for Climate Models

items.summary: Chen, Golosov and Krasikov study taxation in matching environments where sorting and surplus sharing are endogenous. Their approach uses matching elasticities to characterize equilibrium adjustments from tax reforms, applied to a family formation model that links responses to complementarities as Becker (1973) emphasized.
items.title: Beckerian Theory of Taxation by Chen, Golosov and Krasikov

items.summary: A NSW supreme court jury heard voice notes sent by Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, the day after he allegedly shot and killed Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon on 19 February 2024. The recordings were played to the jury during his double murder trial. His defence team says the pair died in separate struggles while he acted in self-defence. Defence lawyer John Stratton SC said Lamarre-Condon panicked considerably after the shooting and cleaned up the scene.
items.title: Murder defendant plays voice notes showing mental state in court

items.summary: The US reportedly launched limited, defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island late Monday, hours after Vice President JD Vance expressed optimism about diplomatic progress. Iranian state media reported explosions but called the cause unclear; local outlets and Central Command declined to comment. The attacks came before crucial midterm elections that Trump's party faces over rising costs.
items.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island amid optimism for a deal

items.summary: Analysts expect State Bank of India’s second-quarter standalone net profit to rise about 45 per cent year-on-year, driven by stake-sale gains from share sales in SBI Mutual Fund and NSE. Motilal Oswal Financial Services projects a top estimate of ₹25,250 crore with Net Interest Income growth at 11.3 per cent yoy to ₹47,847 crore, while Systematix forecasts the lower end at ₹23,539 crore. The Bank will declare results later on November 3, 2026.
items.title: SBI Profit Forecast Rises on Stake Sales

items.summary: Walt Disney Co. is moving toward thousands of job cuts, with managers asked to target 20% in annual cost savings, according to people familiar with the matter. The savings may come from job eliminations and expense reductions, though a Disney representative declined to comment.
items.title: Disney Plans Thousands of Layoffs Amid Cost-Cutting Push

items.summary: Mediacorp host Quan Yifeng posted on Instagram that a Xinjiang tour guide mocked and scolded fellow travellers for not buying goods. She said her contract promised no compulsory shopping yet the group visited cotton and jade shops over two mornings, with each purchase reportedly expected to cost at least 2,000 yuan (US$300). Quan bought one piece of Hetian jade but watched others being harassed on the bus. She also complained about long journeys and rest stops where queues were described as worse than amusement parks. Afterward she said she would not recommend visiting Xinjiang.
items.title: Xinjiang tour guide mocked travellers who refused to shop, host says

items.summary: An award ceremony took place at the Imperial Palace in Tokyo on Tuesday for Japan's fiscal 2026 Order of Culture. The government named eight awardees last month; seven attended and received medals from Emperor Naruhito, including Nobel Prize winner Kenso Soai, lighting designer Motoko Ishii, architect Toyoo Ito, biologist Tsuneyoshi Kuroiwa, literature scholar Tetsuya Shiokawa, composer Shunichi Tokura, and immunologist Shigekazu Nagata. Nintendo executive fellow Shigeru Miyamoto was absent from the event held on Culture Day.
items.title: Nintendo's Miyamoto among Order of Culture recipients who skipped ceremony

items.summary: Brent crude futures rose 11 cents, or 0.12%, to $105 a barrel on November 3, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 26 cents, or 0.27%, to $97 a barrel. The move followed reports that the United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island, with officials describing the attacks as defensive operations aimed at preventing Iran from targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts said the news added a fresh risk premium after markets had begun pricing in a diplomatic resolution. Goldman Sachs raised its forecasts, warning Brent could reach $140 by 2027 if Gulf production stays well below average.
items.title: Crude oil rebounds as US strikes Iran weigh on supply outlook

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, ten stocks in the Nifty200 pack had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on November 2, 2026. The 200-day moving average is used by traders as a key indicator for determining overall trend direction.
items.title: Ten Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary: Jon Gray, Blackstone president, said on Tuesday that more global equity fundraising is needed to meet likely demand from the AI industry's growth. Speaking at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit in Hong Kong on Nov 3, he cited Meta, Google and Oracle raising equity, plus SpaceX and Anthropic going public, as companies expected to raise capital. Gray said most major tech firms would follow, driven by extraordinary demand for computing power where demand runs ahead of supply. He expressed conviction that this gives comfort despite recent pressure on global tech stocks from AI spending concerns.
items.title: Blackstone's Jon Gray Foresees More Tech Equity Fundraising Amid AI Demand

items.summary: The article profiles several people who rummage through commercial bins for usable items, driven by savings, charity or disgust at waste. Darryl Baker of north London takes clothing from supermarket dumpsters after staff grant permission, estimating she has saved hundreds of pounds in six months. Texan Jeff Ferrell has dived for over 50 years and estimates his finds are worth tens of thousands of dollars a year. Millie Diamond refashions salvaged fabrics into dresses, one estimated at £600, while Charlotte Bayford says she has not bought shampoo for eight years. The practice may be illegal in some US cities but is often tolerated where goods are genuinely discarded or permission is given. Each figure is stated by the person involved or reported without a named source.
items.title: People Salvage Clothing and Goods from Commercial Bins

items.summary: Western Australia women's interests minister Simone McGurk detailed misogynistic abuse against her and staff, saying it has not eased since the Helen Haines incident. She described threats including 'kill yourself' messages to a young staffer, following an alleged attack that left MP Helen Haines with amputated legs. McGurk said online hatred is frightening but insisted social media engagement remains necessary for connecting with electorates.
items.title: WA minister details abuse after Haines attack

items.summary: CanTEST, Canberra's drug-checking service, detected medetomidine — a powerful veterinary sedative — in a pill expected to be either benzodiazepine or MDMA. The facility says it is noticing unregulated benzodiazepines turning out to be other potentially dangerous substances instead.
items.title: Canberra Drug-Checking Service Detects Veterinary Sedative in Pills for First Time

items.summary: A reader in London wrote that British Airways mishandled his father’s life-saving dialysis machine twice, damaging and losing it. The Guardian’s Consumer Champions team says the device was too large for cabin baggage but could have travelled on a seat if spare seats were available. BA apologised after being pressed and offered £300 in e-vouchers.
items.title: Guardian consumer champion backs BA over damaged dialysis machine

items.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah claimed on Monday that three crore of the 13 crore voters removed during the special intensive revision were 'Bangladeshi infiltrators.' At a Hyderabad rally, he said more than 6.2 crore had shifted, nearly three crore died and over one crore were duplicates. The Opposition alleges genuine voters were intentionally deleted.
items.title: Amit Shah Claims Deleted Voters Were Bangladeshi Infiltrators
