items.summary: Santosh Davakhar, writer-director-producer of the Marathi film Gondhal (English title Sacred Obsession), is India’s official entry for Best International Feature Film at the Oscars. He self-financed the 1960s-set debut after producers offered lower budgets than expected, spending under Rs 4 crore with GST, and added more on US promotion. Originally released November 14, 2025, it underperformed due to an unknown cast; Davakhar attributes this to low-key marketing. The film will re-release November 13 and compete alongside Angh, with Oscar nominations declared January 17 and the ceremony March 14. Davakhar remains confident of a nomination.
items.title: India’s Oscar Entry Gondhal Bets on All-Risk Gamble

items.summary: Two days of hearings on a legal challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children begin at the country's highest court. A digital rights group will argue that the under-16s rule robs children of free communication, while platform Reddit joins the case separately. The government says it will not be intimidated by legal threats.
items.title: Australia's social media ban faces High Court challenge

items.summary: Air quality across Delhi and the National Capital Region fell into the very poor category, with the overall AQI breaching 300 and crossing 400 in areas such as Rohini and Bawana. In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management enforced GRAP Stage Two measures including higher parking charges, diesel generator curbs, mechanical sweeping, additional metro trips, and Gurugram's work-from-home rules; the Supreme Court permitted only green crackers on limited dates.
items.title: Delhi AQI Enters Very Poor Category, GRAP 2 Imposed Across NCR Ahead Of Diwali

items.summary: Delhi Police ACP Manasvi Vashishta has been suspended after leading a protest outside the police headquarters on Monday, where scores of officers gathered to seek a meeting with Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar. The move follows an indefinite lawyers' strike over alleged threats by the ACP and Shahdara station house officer Arun Kumar in the Lalit Bansal assault case. Vashishta demanded clearer procedures for such matters.
items.title: ACP Manasvi Vashishta Suspended After Leading Delhi Police Protest

items.summary: A survivor statement accessed in the King George's Medical University conversion case alleges sexual abuse and drugging against Dr Rameez, spanning 2012 to 2025. The victim claims she was brainwashed against her religion, impregnated in 2016 with a pressured abortion, and assaulted after confronting him about affairs in 2024. An Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force investigation found Dr Rameez and his family complicit, leading to arrest; the High Court rejected bail.
items.title: Survivor Statement Alleges Abuse in Lucknow KGMU Conversion Case

items.summary: Delhi's overall air quality reached a hazardous level of 451 at 8 am on Tuesday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. Monitoring stations in Rohini (429), Punjabi Bagh (424) and Bawana (408) recorded severe levels, while other areas ranged from very poor to poor. The Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage-II of GRAP across the NCR on Monday, prompting Delhi Police to conduct a checking drive at Ghazipur border as vehicle entry restrictions took effect.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Hazardous Level Before Diwali

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a marital dispute or harsh exchange of words cannot by itself justify terminating a pregnancy, directing the husband opposing his wife's plea to file an affidavit withdrawing allegations made against her. The bench emphasised there was no medical reason for termination and posted the matter for November 4. Earlier, the Bombay High Court dismissed the woman's plea under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, though a medical board had recorded she was in a fragile psychological state. The husband denied circulating WhatsApp messages but withheld evidence to preserve the relationship.
items.title: Supreme Court Bars Abortion Over Marital Dispute

items.summary: The alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has moved beyond police inquiry into a political dispute, with pressure shifting onto current CM DK Shivakumar. Former CM Siddaramaiah met Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal for about 30 minutes and Rahul Gandhi for around 40-45 minutes in New Delhi to raise concerns over the probe, per sources close to him. KPCC chief BK Hariprasad described the operation as “ugly” and urged identification of the real mastermind. HD Kumaraswamy accused Congress leaders of plotting against Siddaramaiah while the BJP stayed away from endorsing allegations directly.
items.title: Congress leaders shift sting-op focus from Kumaraswamy to mastermind

items.summary: A widowed adoptive mother of a 14-year-old boy from Noida has approached the Delhi high court to hand over his custody, alleging aggressive and hypersexual behaviour that left her, her elderly mother and sister fearful. Adopted at six, he is now described as intellectually disabled; she sought institutional placement while offering to contribute toward costs. The case prompts experts on adoption challenges. Santosh Koulagi of the Janapada Seva Trust says returning adopted children happens frequently, estimating 10 unreported cases per publicised one, though he notes this is an estimate rather than official data. CARA reportedly shared figures in 2020 indicating around four to five per cent of children adopted between 2017 and 2019 were returned. Counsel Dr Aloma Lobo says adoption requires effort from parents; Radha Nagesh advocates trauma-informed care and a special committee for difficult placements, while Sheila Ramaswamy stresses the child's welfare must remain central. The court has sought responses from CARA, the Child Welfare Committee and the boy himself.
items.title: Adoptive Mother Seeks Custody Handover for Teen in Delhi Court

items.summary: On Monday, Israeli forces injured two Palestinians near Bethlehem with bruises and demolished a memorial south of Nablus during raids across the occupied West Bank. Troops detained a young man west of Jenin, uprooted olive trees in Al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, blocked roads, closed entrances in Hizma northeast of East Jerusalem, and removed a Palestinian flag from Iktaba. The Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission documented 3,133 attacks by Israeli forces and occupiers in October, up 52.8% from September.
items.title: Israeli Raids Injure Palestinians, Demolish Memorial Across West Bank

items.summary: Fox's $22 billion acquisition of Roku is expected to move forward under a consent decree, according to people familiar with the deliberations. It remains unclear what terms would be involved, and officials said the Justice Department could still change course. The deal had drawn antitrust concerns that rivals feared Fox might favor its own content.
items.title: Fox-Roku Deal Poised to Clear DOJ Scrutiny Under Consent Decree

items.summary: More than 200 families served eviction notices in ward 65 of Tiruchy Corporation besieged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s vehicle and convoy en route to Pudukkottai from the airport, holding placards and slogans demanding justice. The residents have lived over 100 years near a former tannery site allocated for labourers’ housing; the notice claimed private purchase of the land and ordered vacating within 10 days. Over 100 police personnel responded, spoke with protesters, and moved them aside to clear traffic, official sources said.
items.title: Tiruchy Families Block CM Vijay’s Convoy Over Eviction Notice

items.summary: A dispute over Vanavani Matriculation Higher Secondary School, inside IIT-Madras campus, has prompted retired staff member Inbamani to send a 13th petition appealing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The school, founded in 1963 with an initial 50 students and later over 2,600 pupils, now reports enrollment of 1,422 after intake curbs. Petitioners allege systematic winding down and Tamil marginalisation amid enforced Hindi study, seeking government intervention to preserve the institution.
items.title: Vanavani School Petitioners Urge Modi Over Closure Fears

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration seized food stock worth Rs 9. 01 crore during a festive-season crackdown ahead of Diwali, including Patanjali cow ghee from M/s Divya Mahavitarak in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The FDA said 3. 53 lakh kg were confiscated for adulteration and hygiene violations, suspending 19 licences across Mumbai, Amravati and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. It also acted against edible oil from Avenue Supermarts Ltd and issued notices to Tata 1mg Healthcare, ACFO Pharma, Amazon and Flipkart over labelling concerns of Marine Collagen Powder. The drive ran Oct 28-31, seizing banned items worth Rs 79.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Seizes Rs 9.01 Crore of Food in Diwali Crackdown

items.summary: Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, a 20-year-old co-pilot aboard the Learjet 60 that crashed in South Florida while flying from Austin to the Bahamas, was heard repeatedly calling 'Mayday' before impact. Recordings show she reported ice accumulation and temperatures of minus 47 degrees Celsius as the aircraft lost roughly 27,000 feet within a minute. Her mother said she had flown commercially for about nine months but lacked command authority.
items.title: Co-pilot's Final Mayday Call Before Florida Learjet Crash

items.summary: Air pollution in Delhi worsened ahead of Diwali, with the overall Air Quality Index reaching 451 at 8 am on Tuesday, indicating hazardous conditions. Data from the Central Pollution Control Board showed several stations recording severe levels—Rohini (429), Punjabi Bagh (424) and Bawana (408)—while others remained very poor. In response to a pollution spike, the Commission for Air Quality Management invoked Stage-II of GRAP across the National Capital Region on Monday, directing municipal corporations, traffic police and boards in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to enforce sweeping, sprinkling, inspections and hotspot interventions.
items.title: Delhi Air Quality Hits Hazardous Levels as GRAP-II Restrictions Take Effect

items.summary: Control of Great Britain's 39m smart meters has passed to the non-profit Smart Energy Code Company (SECCo), replacing Capita-owned Smart DCC after more than a decade of rising costs and delays. The handover ends a licence granted in 2013, following an investigation into procurement contracts and a £200,000 payment into a consumer redress fund. A spokesperson said the network connects over 39.2m meters across 23m homes with 99.6% availability.
items.title: Non-profit startup takes over control of Britain's smart meter network

items.summary: A competitive Texas governor's race may shape one of the largest US data center markets as AI buildout opposition spreads internationally. Republican Gov. Greg Abbott revised earlier pro-data center policies, while his Democratic opponent pledged a stringent moratorium that could affect about 29% of net capacity additions planned nationally for 2028. Roughly 300-plus state and local moratoriums threaten the US buildout, as Australian and Indonesian projects face similar hurdles.
items.title: US Data Center Opposition Grows Globally

items.summary: NVIDIA says configuring and optimizing Kubernetes for new GPU hardware such as NVIDIA Vera Rubin is complex, because drivers, kernels, runtimes, networking, operators, and schedulers must work together. To simplify this, the NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, captures tuned configurations in reusable recipes that generate bundles for existing deployment tools and validate running clusters. The new Vera Rubin recipe family ships as Preview with training and inference variants validated end to end on a live cluster using GPU Operator v26.7.0 and DRA driver v0.5.0. NVIDIA notes the validation is early: MIG profiles are not covered, some components were never validated together before, one tray was temporarily blocked by a hardware/fabric issue that cleared after reseating, and inference serving performance remains deferred because published runtimes still build against CUDA 13.0.3 rather than the required 13.4.
items.title: NVIDIA Ships AICR Recipes for Kubernetes on Vera Rubin

items.summary: Apple reported stronger-than-expected revenue of $114. 5 billion (€102. 1bn) for the three months to 26 September 2026, driven by record iPhone sales and a services quarter reaching a record $31. 6 billion (€28. 2bn). Both figures beat FactSet estimates, but shares fell around 3% in after-hours trading as investors weighed profit-margin pressure from rising memory chip costs. Apple expects gross margin to fall to between 45% and 46% next quarter, below the 46. 3% analysts had forecast, though it projects revenue growth of 7% to 10%. The company said services growth would slow to 8–9%, from 9. 8% in the September quarter.
items.title: Apple beats earnings forecasts but warns of rising chip costs

items.summary: Microsoft is selling its first US investment-grade bonds since 2017, raising about $25 billion through notes priced in 10 tranches with maturities from 2028 to 2066. Investor orders reached approximately $115 billion, around 4.6 times the amount sought, according to people familiar with the transaction. The company forecasts capital expenditure of around $175 billion for 2026 as it expands AI infrastructure and cloud services. Microsoft Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood noted demand for Azure exceeds supply. The sale is separate from a voluntary employee exit programme covering up to 60,000 staff; the firm expects about 3,000 or fewer acceptances.
items.title: Microsoft Sells $25 Billion in Bonds Amid AI Spending

items.summary: Apple Inc announced an all-time record quarter for the September-ending period, led by $114.4 billion quarterly revenue up 12 per cent year-on-year and iPhone revenue of $57.5 billion growing 17 per cent y-o-y despite supply constraints. Services reached a record $31.6 billion while Mac rose to $10.7 billion on MacBook strength.
items.title: Apple Reports Record Quarter in India Amid Global Revenue Growth

items.summary: Adani Group, controlled by Gautam Adani, is reportedly seeking about $1.5 billion to help finance its expansion into data centers, according to people familiar with the matter. The group plans talks with lenders including DBS, First Abu Dhabi Bank and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial, while also discussing terms with Natixis, ING and Societe Generale. Pricing discussions are ongoing and loan details remain unfinalized.
items.title: Adani Group Seeks $1.5 Billion for Data Center Expansion

items.summary: After the iOS 27 update, some iPhones use roughly 9 to 16 GB for Apple Intelligence even when it is turned off. GSMArena reports changing Siri's language can free storage down to about 100 MB, though this may disable features and is not an official fix.
items.title: iOS 27 Apple Intelligence Uses Up To 16GB iPhone Storage

items.summary: Apple's foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, launched on October 23 after a month of previews and reportedly drew unprecedented demand. The company reported strong fourth-quarter fiscal-2026 results but admitted it cannot meet customer orders for the device. CEO John Ternus said there is no timeline for when supply can catch up to demand.
items.title: Apple CEO Says iPhone Duo Demand Outpaces Supply With No Catch-Up Date

items.summary: The International Energy Agency warned Tuesday that Europe is entering winter with its lowest natural gas reserves since 2013, which could extend market pressure into 2027. Storage reservoirs were about 75 percent full at the end of October, below the European Union's minimum target of 80 percent and the IEA's own estimate that injection was roughly four percent below the five-year average. The agency cited damage to Gulf liquifaction facilities in a US-Iran war, reduced transit through the Strait of Hormuz, and early spring filling as contributing factors.
items.title: Europe Enters Winter with Lowest Gas Reserves Since 2013

items.summary: Google has added Dreambeans to its portfolio as a bespoke AI visual feed drawing on users’ own context rather than generic artificial intelligence (AI) generated images. The feed relies on Google Gemini’s Personal Intelligence capabilities across apps such as Gmail, Drive, Photos, YouTube and Search services, with those connections optional during setup. Gozde Oznur of Google Labs describes the vision as a proactive “handcrafted visual journey” that does not require prompting. Dreambeans currently supports 14 languages, marks India as its first international expansion outside the US, updates three times daily and integrates an embedded chatbot for follow-up questions.
items.title: Google launches Dreambeans, an AI visual feed built on personal context

items.summary: According to The Information, Apple is developing a miniature home robot built around an enlarged HomeView smart display. A prototype would feature a 9-inch screen on a swivelling arm, cameras and sensors for autonomous operation, echoing the iMac G4 and Pixar's Luxo Jr. Design reportedly reached about $1,000 in the US with a possible 2027 launch.
items.title: Apple reportedly developing home robot with swivelling screen

items.summary: ST Headstart is a weekly newsletter from The Straits Times, published every Tuesday noon with career, personal finance and lifestyle coverage. It offers advice on handling passive-aggressive remarks from bosses by responding to their words rather than tone, notes that Singapore stocks have outperformed Wall Street over the past five years through ETFs, REITs, Savings Bonds and T-bills explained by Sue-Ann and Kai Wen with Emelia Tan of Singapore Exchange, points readers to a Headstart On Record podcast, lists Singapore's best workplaces, and shares that Lego bricks withstand compression better than concrete.
items.title: Straits Times Headstart Offers Career and Money Tips

items.summary: Apple posted an all-time record for its September quarter revenue in India, with iPhone 17 leading Q3 shipments there and globally. Apple CEO John Ternus said the company set records across developed and emerging markets worldwide. Analyst Tarun Pathak of Counterpoint Research noted rising consumer spending and easy financing are driving purchases even as overall smartphone sales soften. Services also hit an all-time record at $31.6 billion, up 10 per cent year-over-year.
items.title: Apple Reports Record September Quarter Revenue in India

items.summary: The People's Bank of China raised its foreign exchange reserve requirement ratio by 2 percentage points to 6% on Nov 3, effective Nov 15, in the strongest move yet to slow a yuan rally. The change would withdraw an extra US$24 billion from the financial system and followed the currency weakening as much as 0.37% to 6.6728 per dollar. Analysts say it carries symbolic significance but may not ease oversupply.
items.title: PBOC Raises FX Reserve Requirement as Yuan Hits Six-Month Low

items.summary: Gujarat-based Rayzon Solar Ltd is set to begin production at its 5.1 GW TOPCon solar cell facility in December 2026, with initial deliveries expected in the first quarter of 2027. The move extends the company beyond module manufacturing toward backward integration and reduced reliance on imported cells. Co-founder Chirag Nakrani called it an important milestone; Hardik Kothiya emphasized strengthening domestic capabilities and reducing import dependence.
items.title: Rayzon Solar Commences TOPCon Cell Production in December

items.summary: A major bridge on the Yan'an-Yulin high-speed railway in Shaanxi Province was successfully joined on November 1, marking a construction milestone. The Qingjian River Bridge spans 670.55 meters across the river using continuous girders built with the balanced cantilever method and vertical excavation supported by steel sheet piles to manage loess terrain risks. Zhang Li, chief engineer of the project, said these measures ensured quality and timely completion.
items.title: Bridge Joins Northwest China High-Speed Railway Line

items.summary: Indian crude-sensitive equities rose on a session in which Brent fell to $104.43 and WTI to $96.30, the article reports. IndiGo shares jumped 4% to Rs 5,118 while Bharat Petroleum gained 3% to Rs 301; Hindustan Petroleum rose 3.5% to Rs 361 and Indian Oil up 3%. Upstream stocks ONGC and Oil India fell up to 2%. Downstream margins are squeezed when crude rises but product prices lag, the piece explains. Goldman Sachs raised its Brent forecast to $105 in December from $90, warning of a possible rise toward $140 by 2027 on Gulf supply risk; JPMorgan said it remains hard to judge how the conflict will play out.
items.title: Crude-sensitive stocks rally as oil dips below $105 a barrel

items.summary: At IBS Pack Prints in Kisumu, Chinese-made machinery now forms the backbone of packaging production for printing, processing and cutting materials. Administration director Beatrice Omari says roughly 99% of the machines come from China, along with raw materials such as CPP and PET, while engineers traveled to Kenya to install and commission equipment before handing it over locally. Production manager Eric Onyango notes that automation has simplified tasks once done by hand but requires technical knowledge to operate and maintain. The company supplies packaging for bread, tea, sugar, water, ice cream and beans across western Kenya, though operators face challenges from high costs, imported materials and power surges that halt production.
items.title: Chinese Machinery Reshapes Kenya's Packaging Sector at IBS Pack Prints

items.summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending an INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Quoted by news agency ANI, he said she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi out of 'utter helplessness', alleging her party had lost ground and that she no longer held elected office. Ghosh also attacked Banerjee over objections to the electoral process, claiming parties must respect public mandates. Separately, he outlined festive-season security arrangements across West Bengal and criticised development boards formed during her tenure for lacking funds.
items.title: Dilip Ghosh Attacks Mamata Over INDIA Bloc Rally and Leadership Shift

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs called for an immediate de-escalation of tensions and the conclusion of ongoing negotiations to reach a diplomatic solution. The MEA condemned an attack on a commercial vessel off Oman's coast that killed one Indian national, Priyanka Jaiswal, and left 13 others rescued. The vessel MSV Al Jusufi came under attack near Limah on Monday evening.
items.title: 'Targeting civilian infrastructure must end': MEA after Indian national killed in attack on ship in Oman

items.summary: Zhao Leji, chairman of China's National People's Congress Standing Committee, held talks with Russian Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matviyenko at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on November 2, 2026. Zhao said China is ready to strengthen strategic communication and deepen cooperation across trade, energy, frontier technologies, and legislative exchanges, taking prior consensus between the two heads of state as its guiding basis.
items.title: China's Top Legislator Meets Russian Federation Council Speaker in Beijing

items.summary: China's top legislature began deliberating a draft law on combating cross-border corruption, which includes promoting a fair and equitable global anti-corruption governance system. Submitted for second reading at the NPC Standing Committee session running through Friday, the draft elaborates legislative purpose and principles, requiring strict adherence to the Constitution and human-rights protection. It sets six chapters and 47 articles, mandates confidentiality of state secrets and personal information, and requires Chinese companies operating abroad to establish integrity departments based on size and risk. Officials cite Operation Sky Net since 2015, which repatriated 14,048 fugitives from more than 120 countries and recovered 66.
items.title: China Advances Draft Law Against Cross-Border Corruption

items.summary: A report dated Nov 2, 2026 examines how Meta’s content moderation in India has become automated and proactive amid state censorship. Following the rise of the satirical Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), whose Instagram page reportedly reached 24.8 million followers, authorities increasingly used takedown orders premised on alleged violations of IT rules. Amendments effective February mandate compliance within three hours via the Sahyog portal; Meta has reportedly connected its systems directly to it so requests are processed automatically without employee review. In the first half of 2026, Meta restricted over 5.4 million pieces of content based on Indian law—more than around 41,000 in the prior six months—most proactively and often citing only an “automated system” or a vague “legal request,” with no appeal option. The author frames this as streamlining state censorship rather than merely complying with it.
items.title: Meta Automates Content Removal in India Under New Rules

items.summary: Corbeil and Ferentinos argue that election integrity on social media is a product-design problem, not only a content-policy one. They propose five relevant affordances—distribution, content, formats, interaction, identity, and monetization—and three broad platform architectures: recommendation systems, social graph networks, and open or federated services. None of these is inherently safer; each redistributes risk differently, so interventions must be tailored to architecture rather than transferred across platforms. Two 2024 cases illustrate the point: a Kentucky voting-machine video that reached 6.1 million views on TikTok before officials found no vote switching, and an AI-generated ad targeting Texas candidate James Talarico that gained more than 850,000 views after larger accounts amplified it 12 hours later. They recommend mapping how information moves through a product, building platform-specific threat models, and treating enforcement as part of a broader system with cross-platform coordination rather than uniform rules.
items.title: No One-Size-Fits-All Election Integrity Playbook for Social Platforms

items.summary: Lawyers for Reddit argued before the High Court on Tuesday that the Australian government's rushed passage of its under-16s social media ban legislation in 2024 produced ill-thought-out, over-broad laws. The company contends the ban impinges the implied freedom of political communication by preventing teenagers from posting or commenting while still allowing them to view content. Reddit announced the challenge after eSafety included it in the ban despite its dispute that it meets the law's definition of a social media platform. Lawyers say the legislation fails to address specific risk factors and would be better handled through alternative measures already before parliament.
items.title: Reddit challenges Australia's under-16 social media ban in high court

items.summary: Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock said "some pain now will prevent even worse pain down the track" after lifting official interest rates to an 18-year high of 4.85%, the bank's fifth increase in 2026, aimed at persistent inflation. The decision split the board and intensified pressure on over 3.3m mortgage holders. In its Statement on Monetary Policy, the RBA projected a cost-of-living crisis lasting another year, with inflation returning below target only by late next year. Economists from UBS read the softer language as "clearly dovish," suggesting rates may hold in the short term.
items.title: RBA hikes rates for fifth time as Bullock warns of near-term pain

items.summary: Surrey County Council has launched its annual Warm Welcome scheme for autumn and winter, offering free hot drinks at community venues and libraries until 31 March 2027. The service runs in over 100 venues across Surrey and has operated since 2022. Mark Nuti, cabinet member for health, wellbeing and public health, said keeping warm at home had become a challenge and no-one should feel isolated or cold alone.
items.title: Surrey County Council launches annual Warm Welcome scheme

items.summary: A senior Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor, Ravinder Dhillon, cited a legal case that did not exist while arguing for the prosecution of an 11-year-old boy accused of raping his seven-year-old sister. The fictitious citation appeared to come from an AI response during internet research and was admitted in error after October. Brian Flanagan, an expert on AI and law at Maynooth University, called it a serious failure that undermines trust in the legal system. The high court said the mistake did not affect the outcome of the boy's challenge, which is set to go to trial later this week.
items.title: CPS Prosecutor Cites Fictional Case in High Court

items.summary: Financial markets are under pressure from wars, high sovereign debt and trade tensions. The multitrillion-dollar artificial intelligence investment boom has lifted stocks to record highs and raised expectations for a 3% global growth this year. But investors now worry about market resiliency as Trump's trade policies and the Iran war revive inflation worldwide.
items.title: Global Markets Face Fragility Amid AI Spending and Trade Tensions

items.summary: South Africa and Rwanda have lost duty-free access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which Pretoria had sought to retain. President Donald Trump found both governments engaged in practices inconsistent with eligibility criteria, including barriers threatening national security, per a statement Monday from trade representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer. Tensions worsened over Kigali's role in Congo; South Africa braced for the news as ties frayed since Trump returned to power in 2025.
items.title: South Africa and Rwanda Lose U.S. AGOA Trade Access

items.summary: The Hong Kong Observatory reported a monthly mean temperature of 27.6°C in October, data shown Tuesday (Nov 3). This is up 0.2°C from last year's already record figure for the same period. The observatory noted that weather observations began in 1884. Global forecasters warned months ago this El Nino could become the strongest ever observed.
items.title: Hong Kong Records Hottest October on Record as El Nino Drives Temperatures Up

items.summary: Reddit and a libertarian advocacy group have challenged Australia's law banning large platforms from letting under-16s create accounts, arguing it is ill thought out and restricts political debate. Perry Herzfeld told the High Court that barring minors stops them using key communication tools while most continue online anyway. The government will defend the ban after doubling fines to A$99 million.
items.title: Reddit Challenges Australia's Teen Social Media Ban in High Court

items.summary: Documents obtained by Mongabay and The Guardian under the Freedom of Information Act show British environment officials advised ministers not to engage formally with Vantara, the zoo founded and led by Indian billionaire Anant Ambani. Internal communications from DEFRA cited reputational sensitivities and ongoing compliance proceedings as reasons for cautioning against ministerial contact this summer. Officials raised concerns after Vantara sought falcon imports tied to a £50,000 donation to an unnamed exporter, prompting APHA to treat the transactions as commercial rather than zoological. The zoo has denied wrongdoing; India's top court dismissed similar allegations last year. Data released by British authorities show 152 export and re-export permits issued from October 2023 to September 2026 for CITES Appendix I species, though few were used. Vantara said it had not hired or paid any lobbying firm.
items.title: UK Officials Advised Against Formal Engagement With Vantara Ahead of CITES Meeting

items.summary: A Link Blog post reports on OSINT work by Colsto, who shows how imperceptible plane noise in a video can reveal its location. The method extracts Doppler curves from soundtrack background noise and cross-references them with ADS-B flight data to determine speed, distance, and position based on gaps between flights. The technique is described as widely available online.
items.title: OSINT Method Locates Filmmakers via Aircraft Sound

items.summary: On November 3, 2026, the author announced their October sponsors-only newsletter and offered access to current or new sponsors. The edition covers topics including an inflection point for vibe game development, a rising vulnerability situation, LLM releases, API credits tied to $100+/month subscriptions, tools in use, and software releases. A September issue is available as a preview, and paying $10 keeps readers ahead of the free copy.
items.title: October sponsors-only newsletter

items.summary: A 47-year-old Indian national was killed and two others injured when two helicopters collided while landing near Pheriche village close to Everest base camp in Nepal on Tuesday, the Associated Press reported. The accident occurred during autumn trekking season; an injured New Zealand tourist was flown to Kathmandu for treatment while a Nepali pilot received care locally.
items.title: Indian tourist killed in Nepal helicopter crash

items.summary: An author previews a new Free Press article arguing that economists are losing social status, contrasting the intellectually heavyweight advisers of the 1960s and 1980s with today's environment. The piece cites proposed elimination of National Science Foundation funding for social sciences, declining college enrollments, academia seen as more politicized and left-leaning, and AI models outperforming human economists as reinforcing trends.
items.title: Economists' Declining Status Explored in Free Press Article

items.summary: Chinese manufacturer Gokin Solar introduced a new single-glass back-contact module series, the GK-3-54HGF, aimed at Australian residential and commercial markets. The panels use 108 N-type cells from Aiko and range from 495 W to 510 W across four variants. Gokin claims its platform yields about 6–10% more output than TOPCon per area. All units are CEC certified, with a 25-year product warranty and 30-year performance guarantee covering up to 88.85% of original output at year 30. Availability in Australia is expected from early 2027.
items.title: Gokin Solar Launches Back-Contact Modules for Australia

items.summary: Euronews Next interviewed cybersecurity experts about cyber attacks targeting supermarket fridges and freezers across Belgium, Luxembourg, Estonia, the Netherlands, Ireland, Sweden, and France. Marta Rybczynska of Ygreky suggested state-supported groups are likely responsible for a French attack on October 12 that raised temperatures to as high as 50 degrees Celsius. Pavlina Pavlova of Critical Cyber warned AI could automate attacks at scale, saying 'It will probably get worse before it gets better.'
items.title: Cyberattacks on European supermarket freezers may worsen with AI

items.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers denied his government's budget was driving persistent inflation after the Reserve Bank raised interest rates for the fifth time in 2026. He said budgets were not putting upward pressure on inflation but that they could play a helpful role, promising fresh savings in next month's mid-year budget update. Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock avoided commenting directly on the budget while noting overall demand remained too high and that public demand growth had eased to just 2.1 per cent this year against business investment of 12 per cent. Doubts emerged over $36 billion in NDIS savings flagged as subject to considerable uncertainty, while Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson accused the government of a spending addiction fuelling inflation.
items.title: Chalmers Deflects Inflation Blame as RBA Hikes Rates for Fifth Time

items.summary: The US launched limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, per officials who told CBS and its BBC partner. Iranian agency IRNA reported explosions there Monday. Officials said the strikes followed an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attack on a US aircraft. The action comes ahead of midterms amid Trump's falling polls; he called for no rush to expand strikes but floated hitting Iran nuclear site 'Pickaxe.'
items.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island amid midterm pressure

items.summary: Lawyers for fitness influencer Sam Wood, 46, have filed an appeal after he was refused bail in the Supreme Court on domestic violence offences allegedly committed against his wife Snezana Wood. His legal team has asked the Court of Appeal to expedite a hearing within three weeks and will argue Justice Patrick McCafferty's decision was unreasonable or plainly unjust.
items.title: Sam Wood appeals bail refusal over domestic violence charges

items.summary: Europe's bond markets face a fresh headwind as US technology companies increasingly borrow in European currencies to finance AI spending, boosting corporate debt supply and potentially raising borrowing costs. While tech-related borrowing has lagged the United States, investors see scope for larger issuance across euro, sterling and Swiss franc markets this year. BNP Paribas expects investment-grade net supply to rise 83 per cent to €192 billion ($214 billion) in 2027, with offshore US deals worth €80 billion to €90 billion forming the bulk. ECB President Christine Lagarde said hyperscaler debt has pushed sovereign yields up as investors focus on long-end supply pressure.
items.title: European Bond Markets Brace for AI Debt Wave

items.summary: The US Supreme Court denied a last-minute request from the Trump administration to intervene in California's midterm election vote count, upholding two lower-court rulings. The justice department had sought to set aside 20,000 ballots it alleged may have gone to non-citizens. State officials disputed the accuracy of that list and warned segregation during voting was unfeasible. The decision stands on the eve of midterms that could decide control of Congress for two years.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Administration's Bid to Halt California Vote Count

items.summary: Hindustan Times analysis of weather, air-quality and satellite data says smoke from evening farm fires in Punjab and Haryana was the primary driver pushing Delhi into 'very poor' air on Monday. The AQI rose from 117 on Saturday to 261 on Sunday and reached 324 by Monday's 4 PM bulletin—crossing the 300-mark threshold for the first time this season, a level not seen since February 11. On November 1, overnight PM2.5 averaged 194 micrograms per cubic metre, more than three times India's safe limit of 60. HT found meteorological factors alone do not explain the spike: evening fire counts surged from 17 on October 29 to 90 on November 1, and fine smoke particles made up nearly 60% of particulate matter that night versus roughly 40% in October.
items.title: HT Analysis Links Delhi's Record Haze to Evening Farm Fires

items.summary: Two men, Bhagwan Singh and his brother Pritam Singh, were arrested by Madhya Pradesh’s Special Task Force for allegedly poaching a 19-month-old cheetah cub in Sheopur forests using a muzzle-loading shotgun. The cub died from pellet injuries on October 26 after being found wounded near Kuno National Park. This was the first killing and 25th death of a reintroduced cheetah since India brought them back in 2022, when their total population now stands at 54 animals across two sites.
items.title: Two Arrested Over Poaching of Kuno Cheetah Cub

items.summary: In the years after Japan's defeat, a small Indian community struggled under Allied occupation amid trade restrictions and disrupted livelihoods. The Indian Liaison Mission tracked 164 Indians plus 54 dependents as of its 1949 report, describing their economic condition as 'not satisfactory.' Some traders benefited from an Open General Licence scheme in 1947 that permitted private trading; others profited through the Overseas Supply Store. The community remained divided over clubs and associations, with factions forming new bodies after disputes. By occupation's end on April 28, 1952, some Indians declined to register or acquire Indian citizenship until the 1955 act took effect.
items.title: India's Post-War Community in Occupied Japan

items.summary: President Trump signed an executive order in late September directing government agencies to rename artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence,” a term he selected from a poll. About one month later, the newsletter asks which groups are adopting it. The new wording has spread across many government sites and solicitations, though some agencies still use the old term or add transition banners. Among tech leaders, CNBC found only Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk used “Super Intelligence” consistently on third-quarter earnings calls; others like Sundar Pichai of Google and Jensen Huang referenced it but kept using AI. The author frames the rebrand as a possible loyalty test that could fracture public discussion ahead of midterms tomorrow (October 27).
items.title: Tech Leaders and Government Agencies Weigh In on Trump's Super Intelligence Rebrand

items.summary: Shares of ITC rose after reporting a fall in consolidated net profit to Rs 4,229 crore from Rs 5,187 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Net revenue grew 5% to Rs 20,454 crore, while segment profit declined 27.2% and cigarette volumes fell around 8%. The FMCG business posted its strongest growth in 14 quarters at 16%, supported by digital-first brands growing more than 70%. Brokerages remain divided: Jefferies holds a Buy with a Rs 350 target, Nuvama expects EBIT to improve later in the year, Emkay cut its price to Rs 300 citing weak volumes and budget uncertainty, while DAM Capital maintains a Buy at Rs 355. The article is written by Veer Sharma, not a SEBI-registered analyst.
items.title: ITC Shares Rise on Q2 Results Amid Mixed Guidance

items.summary: National Conference MP Syed Aga Ruhullah resigned his Srinagar Lok Sabha seat and quit the Omar Abdullah-led National Conference, deepening a reported crisis in the party. The resignation followed an ultimatum he issued to the Jammu and Kashmir government over concerns about its reservation policy.
items.title: NC MP Aga Ruhullah resigns from Srinagar Lok Sabha seat amid party crisis

items.summary: Royal Mail unveiled its 2026 Christmas stamp series, featuring five scenes from the Nativity created by graphic designer Gareth Howat and illustrator Rebecca Sutherland. The collection marks the 60th anniversary of the first-ever Christmas special stamp, which appeared in December 1966 after a children's art competition announced by postmaster Tony Benn. David Gold said the stamps aim to add festive magic to greetings sent worldwide.
items.title: Royal Mail Unveils Nativity-Themed Christmas Stamps for 2026

items.summary: SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd listed on October 29, 2026, with its Rs 667.53-crore IPO trading near an 8% premium to the price band of Rs 313-330 per share. The issue comprised a fresh offering aggregating Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale worth Rs 517.53 crore, which let existing shareholders partially offload holdings. Subscription was strong: overall demand reached 9.47 times, with the qualified institutional buyer portion at 18.81 times, non-institutional investors at 12.81 times, and retail at 2.71 times. The company plans to use net proceeds partly to prepay borrowings of Rs 42.23 crore and partly for working capital of Rs 74.92 crore.
items.title: SFC Environmental Technologies Lists at an 8% Premium

items.summary: A female doctor alleged sexual exploitation, assault, blackmail and forced religious conversion against Dr Rameezuddin Nayak and his family at King George's Medical University in Lucknow. Contact began during their MBBS studies in 2012, with the victim claiming drugs were administered, private videos recorded for intimidation, a 2016 abortion, pressure to convert to Islam, and coercion into signing a pre-prepared Nikahnama. The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force found the accused and his family complicit, arrested him, and named multiple professors and department heads who allegedly shielded him.
items.title: STF Names Faculty in Lucknow KGMU Conversion Case; Doctor Jailed

items.summary: In Sausalito, California, a US District Court judge ordered Mackenzie Fotsch to pay Matthew Shroder $66,192.50 in legal fees following his partial success on an anti-SLAPP motion. The dispute arose from litigation over a shared home and included allegations of contract disputes and breach of fiduciary duty. After striking portions of four claims tied to the unlawful-detainer action, Shroder sought $90,010 in attorney fees. Fotsch challenged the amount, proposing limits as low as $3,593 or at most $7,129.50. The court approved reduced amounts across three categories before fixing the final award.
items.title: California Court Awards $66,192.50 in Attorney Fees After Partial SLAPP Victory

items.summary: Bollywood actor Tusshar Kapoor reportedly received an extortion call demanding Rs 5 crore from someone claiming affiliation with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Police transferred the case to specialized units, but a voice sample comparison showed no match, raising doubts about authenticity. The threat follows a separate attack on Tiger Shroff in October.
items.title: Tusshar Kapoor Faces Extortion Threat Linked to Bishnoi Gang Allegations

items.summary: Armed gunmen ambushed a mass transit bus carrying five Nigerian police officers along the Sokoto-Gusau highway and opened fire Monday evening, killing all of them. Abdullahi Faruk, a police spokesperson, confirmed the incident and said the bodies were taken to Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital morgue in Sokoto. The officers had been deployed for security at the APC primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District. The attack underscores persistent insecurity across Nigeria's northwest states.
items.title: Five Nigerian police officers killed in ambush on northwest highway

items.summary: The Hindustan Times morning brief of November 3 presents several national headlines in a five-minute roundup. It reports that an Indian tourist was killed and three others injured after two helicopters collided while landing near Mount Everest on Tuesday, per Inspector Mausam Tamang as reported by The Kathmandu Post. Separately, Union minister of shipping Sarbananda Sonowal said an Indian-flagged cargo vessel Al Jusufi was attacked off Oman; one seafarer died and 13 Indians survived. A third item notes rain alerts in Nilgiris after Cyclone Murasu made landfall near Andhra Pradesh, with IMD forecasting winds weakening to 80–90 kmph by Tuesday afternoon.
items.title: Hindustan Times Morning Brief Covers Nepal Helicopter Crash, Oman Attack and Nilgiris Rain Alert

items.summary: Virat Kohli is close to surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's record for most runs by an Indian batter in ODIs played in New Zealand. Kohli has 514 runs in 11 matches and needs another 139 to top the list, where Tendulkar holds 652 from 18 ODIs. India captain Shubman Gill confirmed a fixed opening four with a flexible approach at Nos. 5 and 6 for their five-match series starting November 4 in Auckland.
items.title: Kohli near Tendulkar ODI run record in New Zealand as Gill sets batting order

items.summary: Thousands of displaced Ethiopians were expected to be registered in Moyale, a Kenyan border city jointly administered by the Somali and Oromia regions. They fled clashes after tensions between those regional leaders erupted on October 20 following a flag dispute at Moyale's border. The people have received temporary international protection status from UNHCR.
items.title: Displaced Ethiopians Await Registration in Kenya

items.summary: A Gujarat-based Indian seafarer, Gandhar Nahim Ajij, died after the Indian-flagged MSV AL JUSUFI was hit by an unidentified aerial object near Oman on November 2. Union Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said 13 crew members were rescued and repatriation is being arranged through the Indian Embassy in Oman. The incident adds to at least 23 Indian nationals killed since the West Asia conflict began, per Hindustan Times.
items.title: Indian sailor killed when cargo vessel struck off Oman

items.summary: This Morning Briefing from November 3, 2026 summarizes several news items. In the United States, more than 54 million people have already voted early in midterm elections that will decide control of Congress during President Donald Trump's final two years. The US military carried out defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island after Iranian missiles targeted American assets. Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever submitted his resignation to King Philippe over a budget deadlock, but the monarch deferred a decision and announced consultations with coalition leaders amid a €10 billion ($11 billion) shortfall. Separately, Walt Disney is considering cutting thousands of jobs as it faces weaker box office revenue.
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers Midterms, Iran Strikes and Disney Cuts

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay held a roadshow covering about 50 km between Tiruchy airport and Pudukkottai, where crowds sprinkled flowers and showered him with towels bearing TVK colours. He had earlier prayed at the Murugan temple in Mathur with Cabinet colleagues Ramesh and Mohammed Parvez.
items.title: CM Vijay Receives Rousing Reception in Pudukkottai Roadshow

items.summary: Crude oil prices rose after a Wall Street Journal report cited unnamed U.S. officials saying Iran’s Qeshm Island became a target in limited strikes carried out over recent weeks, contradicting earlier coverage about diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. Brent crude traded at $105.26 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate at $97.07 per barrel. Analysts noted fresh headlines alone may struggle to sustain another rally without concrete evidence of supply disruption.
items.title: Oil Prices Rise After Reports of U.S. Strikes on Iran

items.summary: ACP Manasvi Vashishtha was suspended by the Ministry of Home Affairs on November 3, 2026 for leading a protest outside Delhi Police headquarters. Around 150 personnel joined him after departmental action followed an October 23 clash with lawyers at Shahdara police station. The officers demanded reinstatement and action against the lawyers involved; tensions eased once Vashishtha and Inspector Arun Kumar were transferred, ending a multi-day lawyer strike.
items.title: Delhi ACP Suspended After Leading Police Protest Outside Headquarters

items.summary: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit overnight by cyber attacks broadcasting fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes, before the systems were brought back under control. Sharon Gaffney spoke with Dr Melanie Garson at University College London, who said these kinds of attacks are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust.
items.title: Expert says emergency alerts hacking aims to undermine trust in government

items.summary: The Bombay High Court granted bail on Monday to Santosh Ramesh Sawant, a 52-year-old BEST driver arrested after an electric bus crashed in Bhandup on December 29, 2025, killing four people and injuring 12 others. Justice Shyam Chandak noted prima facie material suggesting the driver may not have received required training before operating route 606.
items.title: Bombay HC grants bail to BEST bus driver in Bhandup crash case

items.summary: SWELECT Energy Systems Limited announced up to ₹4.36 crore for its subsidiary SWELECT Radiant Power Private Limited, which operates a 4.5 MWp DC solar plant under a group captive scheme in Kerala. The Investment Committee approved subscription of up to 1,75,000 equity shares at ₹249.23 each. Additional shares go to other investors, reducing SWELECT’s holding from 100% to 74%. The company said the deal is a related party transaction on an arm’s length basis and will support clean energy generation while boosting future turnover.
items.title: SWELECT Energy Invests in Kerala Captive Solar Plant

items.summary: An intellectual property tribunal ruled that OpenAI failed to stop a Singapore start-up from registering the name “GemGPT”. Principal assistant registrar Gabriel Ong found sharing the letters GPT was not enough, as ChatGPT and GemGPT were whole names. Porolis Technologies can proceed with its trademark for AI-powered gemstone services and was awarded $10,000 in costs. OpenAI’s five objections were rejected.
items.title: OpenAI Loses Bid to Block GemGPT Trademark in Singapore

items.summary: NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories for cities worldwide, building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and developers a common foundation to build services without each organization managing resources of its own. Partners include ITMAX in Malaysia, scaling SamurAI V2 vision agents across 17,000+ cameras by 2027; Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme for startups; and Linker Vision with MVRDV in Taiwan, whose environmental agents simulate a 15-year urban forest canopy in 10 minutes. Details are to be shared at Smart City Expo World Congress in Barcelona Nov. 3-5, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun. The event runs Nov.
items.title: NVIDIA Expands Physical and Agentic AI Across Cities Worldwide

items.summary: An adviser to the European Union's highest court said on Tuesday that Google's AI chatbot Gemini may infringe copyright rules in certain circumstances. Advocate General Maciej Szpunar stated that reusing a press publisher's publication to generate an answer could violate rights, though copyrighted material used for training large language models remains freely permitted under the text and data mining exception.
items.title: EU Court Adviser Warns Google Gemini May Infringe Copyright Rules

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India relaxed Export Declaration Form compliance for resident individuals exporting services, per a November 2 notification. Such exporters need only supply payment-related information to their authorised dealer bank instead of filing an EDF separately. The amendment applies retrospectively from October 1, 2026. Non-individual exporters may use simplified reporting for inward remittances up to ₹10 lakh per transaction.
items.title: RBI Relaxes EDF Compliance for Individual Service Exporters

items.summary: Huawei Digital Power, Huawei's energy technology unit, notified customers of planned price increases of 5% to 15% across several solar and storage product lines. The company said it had absorbed some extra manufacturing costs but could no longer hold existing prices without risking quality or service. It cited rising commodity, PCB and memory prices since 2025 and did not set an implementation date. Huawei is the latest in a series of Chinese suppliers to raise prices; copper hit $14,700 per metric ton in mid-October.
items.title: Huawei Signals Price Hikes for Solar and Storage Gear

items.summary: Reliance Industries' growth prospects are drawing renewed attention from its latest earnings and the listing of Jio Platforms. Analyst Deven Choksey of Dr Choksey Finserv Private Limited notes that strong refining margins, higher diesel cracks and discounted Venezuelan crude should support Reliance's Oil-to-Chemicals business, while Jio's valuation may unlock value for shareholders through potential dividends from its free cash flows. With EBITDA projected to rise from around ₹2.4–2.5 lakh crore to nearly ₹2.7 lakh crore, refining strength and the Jio valuation are cited as key growth triggers.
items.title: Three Catalysts Shape Reliance Industries Stock Outlook Amid Jio Listing and Refining Strength

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani overtook ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming to become Asia's richest person after a nearly 12% rise in Reliance Industries' stock added $8.5 billion to his wealth on Monday, per the item. His estimated net worth reached $88.8 billion according to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, above Yiming's $84 billion.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani Surpasses Zhang Yiming as Asia's Richest Person After Reliance Stock Surge

items.summary: Apple is rolling out its AI-powered “Audio Intelligence” technology for the Apple Watch into beta testing, initially reaching developers in the iOS 27.3 update after being announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine hardware event in September. The set of four opt-in features lets Series 12 wearers detect important sounds, identify songs via Shazam, catch up on conversations through Live Rewind, and take notes with Siri Recaps. Apple emphasizes privacy safeguards, including not identifying speakers or saving raw audio, automatic deletion of unsaved snippets after 30 seconds, and secure processing that excludes even the company from accessing recorded content.
items.title: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence Features Enter Beta Testing

items.summary: In Chile, returning ancestral land to Mapuche communities led them to replace commercial pine and eucalyptus plantations with grasslands for livestock, yet it produced no measurable gains in carbon storage or biodiversity. The authors examine the economic and environmental impacts of the Fund for Indigenous Land and Water (FTAI), which has returned more than 200,000 hectares to Indigenous control, mostly benefiting Mapuche communities. Restitution shifted land use toward grasslands with a reported 4.5% increase and an 18% decrease in plantation forests over time. However, restitution did not significantly improve carbon sequestration, biodiversity, or erosion control, nor change productivity as measured by the Enhanced Vegetation Index. The authors conclude that preventing initial dispossession may preserve ecosystem services more effectively than restoring heavily modified landscapes later (Jaimovich et al. 2026).
items.title: Chilean land returns empower Mapuche but miss ecological gains

items.summary: Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) announced on Nov 3 that it will fully manage the listing review process from Jan 4, 2027, committing to complete applications within six to eight weeks. The change follows a month-long consultation and aims to streamline submissions through a single electronic portal while MAS retains oversight of disclosure exemptions.
items.title: SGX RegCo Takes Over Listing Review To Speed Up Process

items.summary: PyTorchKR and XCENA co-hosted KVCache Meetup Korea on Sep 30, 2026. Speakers from XCENA, SK hynix, FuriosaAI, and LMCache presented technical talks covering CXL memory expansion, GPU compute and HBM bandwidth bottlenecks, request scheduling for RNGD inference engines, and LMCache's multi-platform cache management layer. Sessions included a Roofline analysis using two H100 GPUs with Llama 3.1 8B on vLLM, where retrieving host cache took about 92 ms versus recomputing at about 900 ms under a 12,370-token prompt. Feedback from 72 survey responses showed the program received 48 positive selections (66.7%), with requests for real production examples and translation support noted by organizers planning future events.
items.title: KVCache Meetup Korea Recap Draws AI Inference Feedback

items.summary: Google has launched Dreambeans, an experimental app available through Google Labs for users aged 18 and above. The app turns details from a user's connected daily activity into personalised illustrated stories overnight, aiming to replace endless social feeds with content that reflects what matters to each person. Stories can cover topics worth exploring, places to visit, arts and crafts activities, things to try and event reminders, built using Google Photos and Nano Banana 2 artwork.
items.title: Google Launches Dreambeans AI App in India

items.summary: Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani overtook ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming to become Asia's richest person, per Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list on Tuesday. His estimated wealth rose 10.5% to $88.8 billion, ranking him 22nd globally. The gain followed a nearly 12% surge in Reliance shares that added more than $19 billion to market capitalisation. Reliance reported its strongest quarterly performance for July-September, with revenue up 28% and net profit climbing 34% to Rs29,550 crore.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani Surpasses Zhang Yiming as Asia's Richest Individual

items.summary: OpenAI has introduced Pando, a new Git-compatible server backend that now serves all development in its monorepo while keeping the standard Git client and protocol. The team reports median push latency fell nearly 80%, roughly five times faster, with daily traffic near one petabyte of Git data. OpenAI built Pando in Rust over about 10 weeks; one engineer designed the core and Codex agents implemented it. It reached production in April 2026 after pushes and fetches slowed by late 2025. All performance figures are self-reported, with no independent benchmark yet, and Pando is not open source.
items.title: OpenAI Ships Pando, a Git Backend That Cuts Push Latency ~80%

items.summary: November 3 is UNESCO's International Day for Biosphere Reserves, which combine biodiversity conservation, research and sustainable development. China hosts 36 reserves; its World Network now covers 797 sites across 145 countries spanning 7.5 million square kilometers, more than 5% of the Earth's terrestrial surface. The review at COP17 found the world remains off track to meet the Kunming-Montreal framework's targets for 2030.
items.title: Biosphere Reserves Link Conservation and Communities on UNESCO's International Day

items.summary: On July 30, 2026, the Transformers library enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) for T5. As a side effect, UMT5's decoder could attend to future tokens during training and peek at answers it was supposed to predict. The bug stayed in main for almost two months before being fixed on September 28. To catch such regressions earlier, the team introduced Model Integration Contracts (MICs): published small fixtures built from real checkpoints that run fast integration tests on cheap CPU runners against recorded baselines. A UMT5 fixture flagged the regression across five months of commits; its runner step took 13.4 seconds on CPU. The approach is still being evaluated, as reported failures do not block PRs and coverage remains partial.
items.title: Hugging Face Adds Model Integration Contracts for Transformers Models

items.summary: Srinagar Lok Sabha member Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi resigned from Parliament and the National Conference on Tuesday, marking a setback for the ruling party. News agency PTI reported he hinted at forming a new party of "honest and compassionate people." His resignation follows growing discontent within NC, with about 25 legislators reportedly demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers within 15 days.
items.title: NC MP Resigns Amid Party Revolt

items.summary: KRBL shares rose roughly 9% after second-quarter net profit jumped about 51% year-on-year to Rs 259 crore from Rs 172 crore. Consolidated revenue climbed around 14% YoY to Rs 1,727.4 crore in Q2FY27 versus Rs 1,511.1 crore a year earlier, driven mainly by higher domestic sales that partly offset weaker exports.
items.title: KRBL Shares Rally on Strong Q2 Profit Jump

items.summary: The Hukou Waterfall on the Yellow River, once shown as muddy and turbulent on China's fourth-series 50-yuan banknote, now presents clear cascading waters. Photographer Lyu Guiming noted that clear cascades have become his main photographic subject over the past decade. The change reflects decades of conservation efforts under Communist Party leadership since 1946. Yellow River Conservancy Commission figures show water quality improved markedly: the proportion of monitoring sections graded Class I to III rose from 59.1% in 2016 to 93.2% in 2025, according to YRCC.
items.title: Yellow River Runs Clearer After Decades of Conservation Efforts

items.summary: Trident reported Q2 net profit of Rs 175 crore, up 93% year-on-year. EBITDA rose 46.5% to Rs 313.7 crore while revenue fell 4%. The towel segment declined as yarn grew. Trident plans a new yarn facility in Dhar with capacity for 1,99,680 spindles and an 80-megawatt renewable energy project.
items.title: Trident shares rally on profit jump and capex plans

items.summary: The BJP targeted All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Tuesday after a video surfaced showing her criticising the Brahmanical system. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared it, calling her Rahul Gandhi's 'poster girl' and accusing her of spreading Hindu hate. The remarks came amid protests against election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral roll irregularities. The undated video could not be independently verified.
items.title: BJP targets AISA president Neha Bora over Hindu remarks

items.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday, November 2, 2026. The two heads of state mapped out a blueprint for deepening their strategic partnership. Li said China is ready to deepen cooperation across oil and gas, clean energy projects, agriculture, aerospace satellites, information and communication, artificial intelligence, and cultural exchanges, while promoting free trade agreement negotiations with the Gulf Cooperation Council.
items.title: Chinese Premier Li Qiang Meets Sultan of Oman on State Visit

items.summary: As midterms approach, Americans cite cost of living as their top concern amid soaring food and fuel prices linked to tariffs and the Iran war. Diesel hit a record $6.52 in September from $3.75 before February, while inflation rose to 3.7% from 3%. Trump's approval has fallen but final polls put it around 38%, with only 29% viewing Democrats positively—suggesting anger may not shift votes. Republicans face defensive races in the heartland; Democrats expect House gains and watch for lessons before 2028, though polls historically overstate Democratic support.
items.title: Midterm Voters Weigh Trump's War and Soaring Prices

items.summary: Virgin Media O2 plans to cut thousands of jobs as part of an £800m cost-cutting drive while tackling its £22bn debt. The company, jointly owned by Liberty Global and Telefónica, said £300m of savings would come from job cuts reducing the wage bill 30% over two years, possibly affecting up to 25% of its 16,000 workforce. Chief executive Lutz Schüler framed the moves as necessary for future growth.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 Announces Thousands of Job Cuts Amid £800m Cost Drive

items.summary: Virgin Media O2 announced thousands of UK job cuts as part of an £800m cost-cutting plan to address its £22bn debt. The company said up to a third of the workforce could be affected, with most losses coming from non-customer-facing roles while AI tools expand use across operations.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 Cuts Thousands of Jobs in Cost Drive

items.summary: The dictionary publisher Collins has named “mogging” its word of the year for 2026, according to copywriter Rachel Quin. The term describes outperforming or making someone look inferior in appearance, confidence or status. Quin said it originated around 2016 in bodybuilding culture before entering everyday slang by 2026.
items.title: Collins Names Mogging Its Word of the Year

items.summary: CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel Alameda, aged 30, died after suffering head and chest injuries in a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second-division match. His condition was described as stable but serious on Monday before worsening neurologically; Spanish media reported cardiac arrest en route to hospital. He passed away at 07:00 GMT (08:00 local time). The club and co-owned opponent Andorra issued statements of condolence, with the family requesting privacy.
items.title: Tenerife Striker Jesus de Miguel Dies After On-Field Collision

items.summary: In an opinion piece dated Nov 2, 2026, Maria Federica Martino Lena argues the European Commission’s new AI Office can expose the judgment calls behind frontier labs’ safety claims without needing more power. Since Aug. 2, 2026, the Office may enforce general-purpose AI obligations under Articles 91, 92 and 93 of the AI Act. Yet she says it enforces against definitions it cannot easily control or compare, because providers still set what “frontier,” “safe” and conclusive evaluation mean. She proposes a regulator-owned public taxonomy that records where value-laden choices occur across a model’s lifecycle, making them legible and contestable rather than hidden as technical facts. The piece cites OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra System Card (§10. 1. 1) on counting refusals as successes, its reduced monitorability under §9, and Anthropic withholding pre-release access to Mythos 5. 1 before Dario Amodei’s “We Must Pace the Frontier” (referenced in sentence s34), where a version number of 5.
items.title: EU AI Office Could Make Frontier Labs’ Safety Judgments Visible

items.summary: The Indian government issued draft rules on September 30, 2026, open for public comment until November 5, 2026. They would let institutional ethics committees approve mild and moderate animal experiments without central approval from the CCSEA, which currently handles most cases above rodents. Critics including PETA India called them backward and said they could significantly weaken protections, citing a conflict of interest since five of nine committee members come from the approving institute, plus subjective severity categories. The draft also permits wild, stray animals and livestock from open markets. Animal rights groups argue lab-bred animals are needed for reliable data. As context, more than 2,300 facilities were registered with the CCSEA as of 2022, and a Grand View Research report estimated the CRO preclinical animal-trial market at $183.3 million in 2023, growing about 11.4% annually through 2030.
items.title: Draft India Rules Would Let Local Committees Approve Mild and Moderate Animal Tests

items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said India aims for defence production of Rs 3 lakh crore and exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029. He noted production rose from Rs 46,429 crore in 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while exports grew from under Rs 2,000 crore to about Rs 40,000 crore. Singh stressed strategic autonomy and indigenous capability at the Jaisalmer Consultative Committee meeting.
items.title: India Targets Record Defence Production and Exports by 2029

items.summary: West Ham United ended Nuno Espirito Santo's tenure on Tuesday after back-to-back defeats left them eighth in the Championship while pursuing a Premier League return. He joined the struggling club in September 2025, but could not prevent relegation to the second tier for the first time since 2011. The Board of Directors said a change was necessary as recruiting a new head coach is already underway.
items.title: West Ham dismiss Nuno Espirito Santo as manager

items.summary: European online fashion retailer Zalando launched its first AI shopping agent on Tuesday, amid concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt online retail after reporting a third-quarter gross profit margin of 38.7 per cent below expectations. Shares fell 5 per cent in early trading. Analysts at Jefferies and JPMorgan cited investments as partly responsible for the shortfall.
items.title: Zalando Debuts AI Shopping Agent Amid Margin Pressure

items.summary: Ayu Yoneda, Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's youngest astronaut at 31, says she wants to broadcast from the moon in Japanese. For decades every lunar transmission has been spoken only in English since Neil Armstrong landed there in 1969. In an interview with The Japan Times, Yoneda said she hopes her words will connect people back home and anyone learning our language.
items.title: Japan's Youngest Astronaut Wants to Speak Japanese on the Moon

items.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions on Rwanda's Ministry of Defense over its role in the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo, following earlier measures against Burundi and the Rwandan army announced on 2 mars 2026. The U.S. State Department justifies these steps by Washington agreements signed on 4 décembre 2025 aimed at ending the war. A doctoral researcher analyzing international sanctions argues the penalties target only Rwanda despite mutual violations, noting academic estimates of their success rate range from about 34 % to roughly 4 %, according to Robert Anthony Pape. The article warns such one-sided pressure may undermine diplomatic credibility and backfire in a region where power dynamics prevail.
items.title: U.S. Sanctions on Rwanda Draw Criticism Over Selectivity

items.summary: China's top diplomat Wang Yi held talks with Musaad bin Mohammed Al-Aiban, Saudi Arabia's Minister of State and National Security Advisor, in Beijing on Monday. Al-Aiban handed over a letter from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to Chinese President Xi Jinping on bilateral relations. Wang said China places its ties with Saudi Arabia among its Middle East diplomatic priorities.
items.title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Holds Talks With Saudi National Security Advisor In Beijing.

items.summary: A report from Georgetown and Duke researchers argues that batteries should be the first choice over gas plants for powering data centers, offering advice to states. The authors note developers are building more than 60 gigawatts of new utility-scale gas plants plus around 90 GW of behind-the-meter generators nationwide, a move they warn could cost money if computing demand fails and worsen climate change. Batteries, the report says, can hedge against stranded asset risk, are cheaper for short-term needs, and avoid costly grid buildouts. A BloombergNEF forecast cited in the piece projects U.S. energy storage deployment surpassing 11,000 gigawatt-hours by 2036, a 30% increase from its prior forecast.
items.title: Georgetown and Duke Report Recommends Batteries for Data Center Power

items.summary: A canceled $20 million EPA grant has left the Native Village of Kotzebue in northwest Alaska without a planned wind energy project, part of hundreds of millions removed from tribal communities by the Department of Government Efficiency. The tribe relies on diesel for 75% of its power and spends about 20% of income on it—more than three times the national low-income average. Two Brookings Institution reports argue that cuts to Inflation Reduction Act funding, including a $468 million DOGE reduction and canceled projects like Hopi Tribe solar grants totaling part of a $7 billion program, reflect long-standing underinvestment rather than isolated policy shifts. Authors call for legislation barring grant cancellations.
items.title: DOGE Cuts Leave Alaska Tribe Without Clean Energy Grant

items.summary: CD Tenerife announced that striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda died on November 3, 2026. He was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a second division match tied 2-2 at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López. De Miguel, then 30 years old, had been taken to Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de Candelaria.
items.title: Tenerife Striker Jesús de Miguel Dies After Match Collision

items.summary: Indian farmer Amarsingh Gushinge, 78, plans to sow wheat and chickpeas but cannot plant either crop because dwindling water supplies follow below-average monsoon rains. Like him, millions of farmers in southern and western India face shortages as they prepare winter crops. The Jalna district around his village received about 48% less rain than average this year, the local weather office has said.
items.title: Weak Monsoon Threatens Winter Crops Across India

items.summary: Todd Russell, a Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor who was trapped underground in 2006 and later received an undisclosed illness diagnosis announced in July 2024, has said he is leaving hospital treatment. He posted that after years of pain, uncertainty and treatments he now feels there are no further options medically or physically, and will see out his days at home surrounded by family.
items.title: Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell leaves hospital amid health battle

items.summary: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's daughter Vivienne has legally changed her surname, becoming known as Vivienne Jolie after filing paperwork in Los Angeles County Superior Court on 12 July. She is the fifth of their six children to drop 'Jolie-Pitt,' following Shiloh, Maddox and Zahara; Pax remains the only child still using the double-barreled name. The split dates from a 2016 airplane altercation in which Pitt allegedly became verbally abusive and physical with one of his kids, though an FBI investigation cleared him of all charges.
items.title: Vivienne Jolie Drops Pitt From Her Surname

items.summary: The authors link point-of-sale and payroll records at 20,000 U.S. firms to study tips. They find that tips are a nearly constant share of revenue, so hourly pay moves with it; when firms begin collecting tips they claw back between 23 and 33 cents per dollar through lower base wages. A calibrated model implies tipping raises job value by about half and firm profit by about 30 percent where customers tip readily.
items.title: Authors describe how tipping shifts worker pay with revenue

items.summary: The Bombay High Court said it was "disturbed" by politicians targeting actor Dia Mirza over a video she shot for the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation urging residents not to light firecrackers on public streets during Diwali. The court directed BMC to re-upload the clip and called objections communal, noting India is secular and festivals belong to everyone.
items.title: HC ‘disturbed’ by politicians’ comments targeting Dia Mirza Diwali video, orders BMC to re-upload it

items.summary: Blackstone rebranded its energy investment fund with the phrase “energy transition” in 2022 after already stopping oil and gas production investing. The fund raised $8.7 billion this year, reportedly turning away an additional $3 billion to stay under a cap. On Wall Street, the term covers natural gas plants, data centers, and rising electricity demand rather than only renewables. Analysts Dan Cohn of the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis and Ryan Loughead of BloombergNEF say investors see these as transition opportunities; some funds include methane despite Blackstone’s fund avoiding oil and gas fields. Critics argue gas is not a credible bridge fuel, and climate groups dispute its role.
items.title: Blackstone’s Energy Transition Fund Keeps Natural Gas and Data Centers in Focus

items.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation removed a video of actor Dia Mirza urging Mumbai residents not to light firecrackers during Diwali, following objections from the Bharatiya Janata Party.
